movies.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
movies.summary: Set during World War II, a frail young man is transformed into a super-soldier and takes on a rogue Nazi-science division bent on world domination, ending with him frozen and lost to time.

beforeWatch.context: The earliest point on the whole timeline, and a clean starting line — it assumes you know nothing at all. Most of it plays as a 1940s war picture: the Second World War is on, America has just entered it, and the fringe science on both sides is running well ahead of the era. The only thing worth carrying in is that this world's history is our history, right up until the point where it isn't.

deepDive.plot: In WWII, scrawny but big-hearted Steve Rogers volunteers for an experimental super-soldier program and becomes Captain America. He spends the rest of the war fighting Hydra's rogue science division, led by the Red Skull, who is chasing a mystical artifact called the Tesseract to power city-destroying weapons. In the climactic battle, Steve crashes an out-of-control plane into the Arctic ice to save the country, and wakes up decades later in the present day, having lost everything and everyone he knew.
deepDive.significance: This is the emotional and thematic starting point of the entire saga — it establishes Captain America's core values (sacrifice, decency, loyalty) that every other Avenger gets measured against, and plants the Tesseract, Hydra, and the 'man out of time' premise that echo through nearly every later film.
deepDive.orderNote: It's placed first in narrative order because, chronologically, it's simply the earliest MCU story — set in the 1940s, decades before every other film on this list.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: Falls from a speeding Hydra train and is presumed dead.
watchFor.future: Secretly recovered and brainwashed by Hydra as the Winter Soldier — reappears in Captain America: The Winter Soldier.

watchFor.name: Red Skull
watchFor.thisFilm: Vanishes after touching the Tesseract's energy, seemingly disintegrated.
watchFor.future: Resurfaces as the guardian of the Soul Stone on Vormir in Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame.

watchFor.name: The Tesseract
watchFor.thisFilm: Recovered from the ocean floor by Howard Stark after the battle.
watchFor.future: Becomes central to Loki's invasion in The Avengers, then the target of a time heist in Avengers: Endgame.

watchFor.name: Peggy Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: Promises to wait for Steve, then loses him to the ice for decades.
watchFor.future: Goes on to help found S.H.I.E.L.D.; remains an emotional throughline for Steve through Avengers: Endgame.

movies.title: Iron Man
movies.summary: A billionaire weapons manufacturer is captured and forced to build a weapon, but instead builds a suit of armor and escapes, setting him on a new path.

beforeWatch.context: This is where the modern-day story actually begins, and the film everything else grows out of. Nothing before it is required — the two period pieces you've just watched are background colour, not setup. Go in expecting a grounded film about weapons manufacturing and one man's very expensive change of heart.

deepDive.plot: Weapons manufacturer Tony Stark is captured by terrorists in Afghanistan and forced to build a weapon; instead, he secretly builds a suit of powered armor and escapes. Back home, he has a change of heart about his company's arms dealing, refines the suit into the Iron Man armor, and exposes and defeats his mentor Obadiah Stane, who tries to steal the technology and kill him.
deepDive.significance: This is the film that started the entire MCU. It establishes the tone (witty, grounded, character-first), Tony Stark as the franchise's flagship personality, and ends with the first hint that a larger team-up is coming.
deepDive.orderNote: Comes third in narrative order because, story-wise, its 2008 'present day' setting happens after Captain America's WWII era and Captain Marvel's 1995 setting, even though it was the very first MCU film ever released.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury / Avengers Initiative
watchFor.thisFilm: Shows up in Tony's home in the film's post-credit scene.
watchFor.future: Reveals the wider 'Avengers Initiative,' seeding the whole team-up storyline.

watchFor.name: "I am Iron Man"
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony publicly reveals himself as Iron Man instead of keeping a secret identity.
watchFor.future: Sets a precedent of openness that shapes how he handles being a hero for the rest of the saga.

movies.title: The Incredible Hulk
movies.summary: A scientist on the run tries to control a rage-fueled transformation caused by a failed experiment, while the military hunts him down.

beforeWatch.context: Runs alongside the previous film rather than after it, and needs nothing from it. One heads-up that isn't a plot point: Bruce Banner is played by a different actor here than in every film that follows, which trips people up if nobody warns them. Treat it as a chase film — he's a fugitive when it opens, and the story is already in motion.

deepDive.plot: Scientist Bruce Banner, on the run and trying to cure the gamma radiation accident that turns him into the Hulk, is relentlessly hunted by the U.S. military under General Ross. After a confrontation with a soldier who injects himself with a similar serum and becomes the monstrous Abomination, Banner reluctantly transforms and defeats him, then goes into hiding, trying to control his condition.
deepDive.significance: Establishes the Hulk as a founding Avenger and introduces General Ross, whose vendetta against Banner (and later political rise) recurs across multiple future phases.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits fourth because its story unfolds in the same rough present-day period as Iron Man, just following a different thread of the world.

watchFor.name: General Ross
watchFor.thisFilm: Leads the military manhunt for Bruce Banner.
watchFor.future: Returns years later as U.S. Secretary of State pushing the Sokovia Accords, and eventually becomes President.
watchFor.spoils: Captain America: Civil War / Brave New World

watchFor.name: Emil Blonsky / Abomination
watchFor.thisFilm: Injected with a version of the super-soldier serum, becoming the monstrous Abomination.
watchFor.future: Resurfaces decades later, imprisoned, in Shang-Chi and She-Hulk: Attorney at Law.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark cameo
watchFor.thisFilm: Meets with General Ross about a 'team' being put together.
watchFor.future: First hint that Stark and the super-soldier program are connected, foreshadowing the Avengers Initiative.

movies.title: Iron Man 2
movies.summary: Facing pressure from the government and a personal crisis, a hero must deal with a new enemy seeking revenge tied to his father's past, while a former ally's ambitions grow.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up about six months after the first film, with Tony now a very public figure and enjoying it far too much. The wider organisation that has been hovering at the edges starts stepping properly into frame here, so this is the first film that feels like it's building toward something larger.

deepDive.plot: With his health failing from palladium poisoning caused by his own arc reactor, Tony Stark faces government pressure to hand over his suit technology, a vengeful new enemy named Ivan Vanko seeking payback for his father's mistreatment by Howard Stark, and a scheming rival arms dealer, Justin Hammer, who backs Vanko's attacks.
deepDive.significance: Cures Tony's health crisis, formally introduces Black Widow and War Machine, and ends with Nick Fury officially recruiting Tony into the Avengers Initiative — a direct bridge into the team-up storyline.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows Iron Man directly since it's a straightforward sequel continuing Tony's ongoing story a couple of years later.

watchFor.name: Black Widow / Natasha Romanoff
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduced as 'Natalie Rushman,' secretly a S.H.I.E.L.D. plant inside Stark Industries.
watchFor.future: Becomes a founding Avenger.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury / S.H.I.E.L.D.
watchFor.thisFilm: Formally recruits Tony into the Avengers Initiative by film's end.
watchFor.future: Sets the team-building plot of The Avengers in motion.

watchFor.name: Mjolnir (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: A S.H.I.E.L.D. team discovers a hammer embedded in a crater in the desert.
watchFor.future: Leads directly into the plot of Thor.

movies.title: Thor
movies.summary: A powerful but arrogant warrior is cast out of his home realm and stripped of his power, learning humility on Earth while a threat brews back home.

beforeWatch.context: The first trip off Earth, and your introduction to Asgard — a realm with its own royal family, its own politics and a very long history that the films treat as fact rather than myth. It works cold; nothing from the previous films is needed. Expect a fish-out-of-water story once it reaches Earth.

deepDive.plot: Arrogant Asgardian prince Thor is stripped of his power and banished to Earth by his father Odin as punishment for reigniting an ancient war. Humbled by his time among humans, he earns back his hammer Mjolnir and returns home just in time to stop his adopted brother Loki, who has seized the throne and nearly destroyed a rival realm to prove himself.
deepDive.significance: Opens up the cosmic/godlike side of the MCU and introduces Loki, who becomes one of the franchise's most important recurring characters and eventually one of its best villains-turned-heroes.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed sixth because its story wraps up right before The Avengers, with Loki's escape directly setting up that film's plot.

watchFor.name: Loki
watchFor.thisFilm: Learns the truth about his heritage and falls into the void after losing his claim to the throne.
watchFor.future: Resurfaces as the villain of The Avengers.

watchFor.name: Hawkeye (cameo)
watchFor.thisFilm: Appears briefly as a S.H.I.E.L.D. sniper watching Thor.
watchFor.future: Joins the team properly in The Avengers.

watchFor.name: The Tesseract (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Nick Fury tells Loki (through a possessed Selvig) it's 'more than power.'
watchFor.future: Sets up an outside force manipulating Loki's actions in The Avengers.

movies.title: The Avengers
movies.summary: A team of powerful individuals is assembled to stop a stolen artifact from being used to open a portal for an invading force.

beforeWatch.context: The payoff the whole phase has been quietly building toward, and the one film here that genuinely expects you to have done the reading. Everyone arrives with baggage from their own film and none of it gets re-explained. You'll get the most out of it if the four solo films are fresh, and if you remember that the organisation running the operation has been recruiting since the very first post-credits scene you saw.

deepDive.plot: After Loki steals the Tesseract and a mind-controlling scepter, Nick Fury assembles Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye to stop him before he can open a portal for an alien invasion force called the Chitauri. The team, initially fractured by ego and mistrust, comes together in New York to close the portal and defeat the invasion, cementing them as Earth's protectors.
deepDive.significance: The culmination of Phase One — this is the movie that proved a shared cinematic universe could actually work, and it sets the template (a team-up event capping each phase) that the franchise repeats for over a decade.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed last because it's the direct payoff of every setup planted in the previous six films — Loki's arc, the Tesseract, and each hero's introduction all converge here.

watchFor.name: Loki's scepter
watchFor.thisFilm: Used to control minds and open the portal for the Chitauri invasion.
watchFor.future: Later revealed to contain the Mind Stone — becomes Vision, and gives Wanda and Pietro their powers, in Age of Ultron.

watchFor.name: Thanos (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Shown smiling after learning of the Chitauri's defeat.
watchFor.future: First tease of the Mad Titan, who becomes the driving antagonist of the whole Infinity Saga.

watchFor.name: Loki's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Captured and placed in chains for the trip back to Asgard.
watchFor.future: Sets up Thor: The Dark World, where he escapes custody again.

movies.title: Iron Man 3
movies.summary: In the aftermath of New York, Tony Stark grapples with anxiety while a terrorist calling himself the Mandarin targets him, drawing him into a conspiracy involving a rogue scientist's super-soldier program.

beforeWatch.context: Set at Christmas, roughly six months after the Battle of New York, and the first film to deal with the aftermath of that fight rather than the fight itself. Tony is not okay, and the film treats that as its actual subject. Everything you need about the invasion comes from the previous film.

deepDive.plot: Tony Stark, suffering panic attacks after the wormhole battle in New York, obsessively builds Iron Man suits while a terrorist calling himself the Mandarin bombs targets across the country. After his home is destroyed, Tony discovers the Mandarin is actually a washed-up actor, and the real threat is Aldrich Killian, a scientist using an unstable regenerative serum called Extremis to create super-soldiers — including a version of Pepper Potts he kidnaps and injects. Tony destroys the Extremis operation, has the shrapnel and reactor removed from his chest, and quietly decides to stop defining himself by the suit.
deepDive.significance: Closes out Tony's personal arc from the first Iron Man trilogy — dealing with PTSD and an overreliance on the armor — while quietly seeding a future MCU villain organization through Trevor Slattery.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Two because it's the first story to deal with life after The Avengers, picking up just months later at Christmas.

watchFor.name: Trevor Slattery
watchFor.thisFilm: Revealed to be a washed-up actor hired to play a fake 'Mandarin' as a media distraction.
watchFor.future: Later abducted by the real Ten Rings organization, reappearing years later in Shang-Chi.
watchFor.spoils: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

watchFor.name: Tony's arc reactor removal
watchFor.thisFilm: Has the shrapnel and reactor removed from his chest by the end of the film.
watchFor.future: Changes the design and necessity of his suits going forward.

movies.title: Thor: The Dark World
movies.summary: An ancient race led by the vengeful Malekith returns to plunge the universe into darkness using a weapon called the Aether, forcing Thor to make an uneasy alliance with Loki to save the Nine Realms.

beforeWatch.context: Thor has spent the time since New York putting out fires across the realms, and Asgard is dealing with the fallout of the first film's ending. Jane Foster has been off-screen the whole time and the film picks her thread back up. Both previous Thor-related films matter more than usual here.

deepDive.plot: An ancient race of Dark Elves led by Malekith awakens after millennia of dormancy, seeking to use a reality-warping substance called the Aether to plunge the universe back into darkness. When Jane Foster accidentally becomes host to the Aether, Malekith's forces attack Asgard and kill Thor's mother Frigga. Thor breaks Loki out of prison to smuggle Jane through the Nine Realms and defeat Malekith on Earth, at the cost of Asgard being left without its protective shield.
deepDive.significance: Deepens the tragedy of Thor's family with his mother's death, and hands the Aether — a literal Infinity Stone — off to the Collector, continuing the scavenger hunt that defines the whole saga.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows Iron Man 3 as the next Phase Two story chronologically, set in the same rough year.

watchFor.name: The Aether / Reality Stone
watchFor.thisFilm: Handed off to the Collector for safekeeping in the mid-credit scene.
watchFor.future: Later glimpsed in his collection in Guardians of the Galaxy, then eventually claimed by Thanos.
watchFor.spoils: Guardians of the Galaxy / Avengers: Infinity War

watchFor.name: Loki (disguised as Odin)
watchFor.thisFilm: Secretly takes the throne of Asgard in the film's final twist.
watchFor.future: The deception is revisited at the start of Thor: Ragnarok.

movies.title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
movies.summary: Steve Rogers uncovers a conspiracy that has quietly taken root inside S.H.I.E.L.D. itself, and finds himself hunted by a mysterious, deadly assassin known as the Winter Soldier.

beforeWatch.context: Steve is two years into the present day now, working full time for the intelligence agency you've watched operate since the first film — and increasingly uneasy about how it does business. This is the most grounded, conspiracy-flavoured film so far, and it assumes you remember both his war-era history and who was running the show in New York.

deepDive.plot: Two years after the Battle of New York, Steve Rogers discovers that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been secretly infiltrated by Hydra from its very founding, using its own helicarriers and a predictive algorithm to preemptively eliminate future threats to Hydra's rule. Steve, Natasha, and new ally Sam Wilson uncover the conspiracy, only to find that the assassin hunting them, the Winter Soldier, is Steve's presumed-dead best friend Bucky Barnes, brainwashed by Hydra for decades. Steve refuses to fight him, the helicarriers are destroyed, and S.H.I.E.L.D. collapses entirely.
deepDive.significance: One of the most consequential films in the franchise — it dismantles S.H.I.E.L.D. as a safety net for every hero going forward, reveals Hydra's decades-long infiltration, and sets Bucky's redemption arc in motion.
deepDive.orderNote: A direct sequel to Cap's arc, unfolding two years after The Avengers — the same rough period as Iron Man 3 and Thor: The Dark World.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes / Winter Soldier
watchFor.thisFilm: Survives the Triskelion's collapse and disappears into hiding.
watchFor.future: His search for redemption drives Captain America: Civil War and beyond.

watchFor.name: Wanda & Pietro Maximoff (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Shown as twins being experimented on by Hydra alongside Loki's scepter.
watchFor.future: Join the fight against Ultron in Avengers: Age of Ultron.

watchFor.name: Hydra's infiltration of S.H.I.E.L.D.
watchFor.thisFilm: Exposed and dismantled, collapsing S.H.I.E.L.D. as an organization.
watchFor.future: Reshapes how the Avengers operate — with no safety net — in every film afterward.

movies.title: Guardians of the Galaxy
movies.summary: A group of misfit outlaws from across the galaxy is forced to band together to stop a fanatical warrior from acquiring a mysterious orb of immense and destructive power.

beforeWatch.context: A hard reset into a completely different corner of the universe, with a new cast who have never heard of anyone you've met so far. You can watch this cold — it explains its own world from scratch. The only thread connecting it to what you've seen is one object that behaves a lot like others you've encountered before.

deepDive.plot: Small-time thief Peter Quill, abducted from Earth as a child, steals a mysterious orb that turns out to be an Infinity Stone, drawing the attention of the fanatical Kree warrior Ronan. Quill is forced into an uneasy alliance with the assassin Gamora, the bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and the vengeful Drax, and together they narrowly stop Ronan from using the Stone to destroy an entire planet, forming an unlikely family in the process.
deepDive.significance: Introduces the cosmic side of the MCU wholesale — a completely new cast and corner of the universe — and is the first film to hand an Infinity Stone directly to an authority (the Nova Corps) rather than a hero, setting up its eventual theft by Thanos.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the first fully cosmic MCU story, set in the same broad period as the Earth-based Phase Two films.

watchFor.name: The Orb / Power Stone
watchFor.thisFilm: Delivered to the Nova Corps for safekeeping after Ronan's defeat.
watchFor.future: The first Infinity Stone the audience watches change hands, foreshadowing Thanos's collection.

watchFor.name: Thanos
watchFor.thisFilm: Appears briefly on-screen receiving news of Ronan's failure.
watchFor.future: Ties the cosmic side of the MCU directly to the coming Avengers films.

watchFor.name: Yondu & Peter Quill's parentage
watchFor.thisFilm: Yondu is shown to have withheld Quill from his real father for unclear reasons.
watchFor.future: Sets up the reveal of his father, Ego, in Vol. 2.

movies.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
movies.summary: Shortly after escaping other galactic factions, the Guardians must survive the appearance of Peter Quill's mysterious birth father while old grudges within the team come to a head. Set only months after the first film, so it's grouped here narratively even though it released during Phase Three.

beforeWatch.context: A couple of months after the first film, with the same crew now working together, badly, as a going concern. It's almost entirely self-contained: no knowledge of Earth's heroes is needed, and the film is much more interested in this crew's family history than in the wider universe.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after the first Guardians film

deepDive.plot: Months after saving the galaxy, the Guardians are hired by the golden Sovereign race, whom they quickly anger, and rescued by a mysterious being who claims to be Peter Quill's father, Ego — a Celestial. Peter is drawn in by the promise of a family and cosmic power, but discovers Ego has been systematically seeding planets with his own offspring and hollowing out worlds (including killing his own children) to eventually reshape the universe in his image. The Guardians kill Ego together, and Peter chooses his found family over his birth father.
deepDive.significance: The emotional core of the whole Guardians trilogy — it reveals Peter's real parentage, gives Yondu a redemptive death, and confirms Mantis and Nebula as part of the team's found-family dynamic going forward.
deepDive.orderNote: Grouped in Phase Two because it's set only months after the first film (2014), even though it released during Phase Three (2017) — narrative timeline over release-phase branding, same reasoning applied elsewhere on this list.

watchFor.name: Adam Warlock's cocoon (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Ayesha vows to create a 'perfect' being to destroy the Guardians.
watchFor.future: Pays off with Adam Warlock's introduction in Vol. 3.

watchFor.name: Kraglin & Yondu's arrow
watchFor.thisFilm: Kraglin inherits Yondu's fin and signature weapon after his death.
watchFor.future: Stays relevant to Kraglin's role in later Guardians appearances.

watchFor.name: Groot's growth
watchFor.thisFilm: Baby Groot begins growing throughout the film.
watchFor.future: Ages into the teenage Groot seen in Infinity War and Endgame.

postCredit.timing: The five scenes are scattered throughout the credits rather than bunched at the start or end — check back periodically instead of waiting for one big moment at the very finish.

movies.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
movies.summary: Tony Stark's attempt to build a peacekeeping artificial intelligence backfires when it becomes the villainous Ultron, forcing the Avengers to confront a new threat alongside a pair of enhanced siblings.

beforeWatch.context: The band is back together and has been operating as a unit for a while when this opens — the film drops you into an ongoing campaign rather than reassembling everyone. It leans on the collapse of the organisation from The Winter Soldier and on Tony's state of mind after Iron Man 3, so both are worth having fresh.

deepDive.plot: A year after Winter Soldier, the Avengers raid a Hydra base and recover Loki's scepter, inside which Tony Stark and Bruce Banner discover an artificial intelligence they use to build a global peacekeeping program, Ultron. Ultron immediately concludes humanity itself is the threat to peace and tries to trigger an extinction-level event using a floating city and a vibranium-powered synthetic body. The Avengers, aided by two enhanced Hydra experiments (Wanda and Pietro Maximoff), stop Ultron, though Pietro is killed and a new synthetic being, Vision, is created from the very body Ultron built for himself.
deepDive.significance: The last time the original six Avengers are together as a fully unified team before the roster — and the team's trust in each other — starts to fracture; also introduces Vision and Wanda as core, ongoing members of the franchise.
deepDive.orderNote: Caps the Phase Two Avengers-adjacent storylines a year after Winter Soldier, directly before the roster shakeup of Civil War.

watchFor.name: Vision & the Mind Stone
watchFor.thisFilm: Created using Loki's scepter and its Mind Stone, then joins the Avengers.
watchFor.future: Later hunted by Thanos specifically for the Mind Stone in Infinity War.

watchFor.name: Wanda Maximoff
watchFor.thisFilm: Joins the Avengers permanently after her brother Pietro's death.
watchFor.future: Her grief becomes the central subject of WandaVision.

watchFor.name: Thanos and the Gauntlet (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Thanos puts on the Infinity Gauntlet himself, done waiting on subordinates.
watchFor.future: Sets the endgame of the whole saga in motion.

watchFor.name: Wakanda / vibranium
watchFor.thisFilm: Ultron's body is forged from vibranium sourced from Wakanda.
watchFor.future: First real spotlight on Wakanda, foreshadowing Black Panther.

movies.title: Doctor Strange
movies.summary: A brilliant but arrogant surgeon loses the use of his hands in an accident and seeks healing in the mystic arts, discovering a hidden world of sorcery and a looming threat from another dimension.

beforeWatch.context: A standalone origin story that opens the door on magic, which the films have not seriously dealt with until now. Nothing prior is required. It runs roughly parallel to the films around it rather than after them, so don't worry about slotting it precisely.

deepDive.plot: Brilliant but arrogant surgeon Stephen Strange loses the use of his hands in a car accident and, out of desperation, seeks out a mystical order in Kathmandu led by the Ancient One. He masters the mystic arts faster than anyone before him, only to discover a rogue former student, Kaecilius, is trying to merge Earth with a dark dimension ruled by the entity Dormammu. Strange traps Dormammu in a time loop using the Time Stone to force a bargain, saving Earth and choosing to become the new Sorcerer Supreme.
deepDive.significance: Introduces magic and the multiverse as a real, functioning part of the MCU, and hands Earth its second major Infinity Stone guardian — setting up Strange as one of the most important players in the Infinity Saga's endgame.
deepDive.orderNote: Set the same year as Civil War, but its story is self-contained, so it's placed here as a natural thematic grouping within Phase Three rather than a tight timeline link.

watchFor.name: The Time Stone
watchFor.thisFilm: Kept in the Eye of Agamotto, used to defeat Dormammu.
watchFor.future: Becomes one of the most critical Infinity Stones in Infinity War's ending and Endgame's time heist.

watchFor.name: Thor cameo (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Strange offers to help Thor track down Odin.
watchFor.future: Leads directly into the plot of Thor: Ragnarok.

watchFor.name: Mordo (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Leaves the order, disillusioned with how casually sorcerers bend natural law.
watchFor.future: Becomes a quiet antagonist thread for future Doctor Strange stories.

movies.title: Ant-Man
movies.summary: Con man Scott Lang is recruited by scientist Hank Pym to master a suit that lets him shrink to the size of an insect, using his new ability to pull off a heist that could save the world.

beforeWatch.context: A deliberately small film — a heist story about one family, set in a world where the big team exists but is busy elsewhere. It stands alone almost completely, and it's the first film in a while that isn't about saving the planet. A little familiarity with the wider world helps one or two jokes land, nothing more.

deepDive.plot: Recently released ex-con Scott Lang is recruited by scientist Hank Pym to become the new Ant-Man, using a size-changing suit Pym has kept hidden for decades. Pym's plan is to stop his former protégé, Darren Cross, from replicating and weaponizing the same shrinking technology as the Yellowjacket. Scott pulls off a heist inside Cross's own company, defeats Yellowjacket, and earns Hank's trust, while Hank's daughter Hope is finally given her mother's old Wasp suit.
deepDive.significance: A smaller-scale, heist-movie palate cleanser after Age of Ultron's stakes, but it quietly plants the Quantum Realm — which becomes the literal mechanism the Avengers use to undo the Snap years later.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed last in Phase Two as the most 'street level' story, unfolding shortly after Age of Ultron with a brief cameo tying Scott into the wider Avengers world.

watchFor.name: Falcon (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Scott tests his shrinking power in a fight against Falcon at the Avengers compound.
watchFor.future: Ties Ant-Man into the wider team ahead of Civil War.

watchFor.name: The Wasp suit (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Hank Pym reveals Hope's late mother's suit, now upgraded for her.
watchFor.future: She becomes the Wasp in Ant-Man and the Wasp.

movies.title: Captain America: Civil War
movies.summary: A government oversight act splits the Avengers into two factions, pitting Captain America and his allies against Iron Man's, while a hidden mastermind quietly manipulates the conflict from the shadows.

beforeWatch.context: The consequences film. Two of the previous films ended with a city badly damaged and a lot of civilians caught in the middle, and the world's governments have finally decided to do something about oversight. It expects you to remember both incidents, and to remember who Steve's oldest friend is and what happened to him.

deepDive.plot: After an Avengers mission in Lagos causes civilian casualties, the United Nations proposes the Sokovia Accords, an oversight framework for enhanced individuals — splitting the team between Tony Stark's faction, which supports regulation, and Steve Rogers', which doesn't. The rift explodes into open conflict when Bucky Barnes is framed for a bombing at the Accords signing, and Zemo — a grieving Sokovian whose family died in Ultron's battle — manipulates both sides into an airport battle, then reveals that a brainwashed Bucky killed Tony's parents years earlier.
deepDive.significance: The biggest fracture in Avengers history until Endgame — it splits the team for years, sends Steve into hiding, introduces both Black Panther and Spider-Man, and sets up the unresolved Tony/Steve rift that Endgame eventually has to pay off.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Three as the direct fallout of Age of Ultron's collateral damage, about a year later.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: Cleared of some crimes but voluntarily frozen in Wakanda to be safe from remaining Hydra triggers.
watchFor.future: Sets up his role in Black Panther and Avengers: Infinity War.

watchFor.name: T'Challa / Black Panther
watchFor.thisFilm: Becomes king of Wakanda after his father's death during the UN bombing.
watchFor.future: Launches directly into his own solo film.

watchFor.name: Peter Parker (Spider-Man)
watchFor.thisFilm: Recruited by Tony Stark for the airport battle — his MCU debut.
watchFor.future: Leads directly into Spider-Man: Homecoming.

watchFor.name: Zemo
watchFor.thisFilm: Achieves his goal of tearing the Avengers apart, then is imprisoned.
watchFor.future: Resurfaces years later as the Baron Zemo of The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.
watchFor.spoils: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

movies.title: Black Widow
movies.summary: A fugitive in the fallout of Civil War, Natasha Romanoff is forced to confront dangerous ties from her past when a mysterious figure threatens to unravel the Red Room program that trained her. Released in Phase Four but set in 2016, so it's grouped here narratively, same reasoning as Captain Marvel and Guardians Vol. 2.

beforeWatch.context: Set immediately after the previous film, in the window where Natasha is a fugitive with nowhere to go. It's a prequel to everything that comes after it in this list, and it finally goes back to the history she has been alluding to since her very first appearance. Released years later, so expect a modern look on an older point in the story.

movies.timeSkip: Set right after Civil War, even though it released in 2021

deepDive.plot: On the run after Civil War, Natasha Romanoff is drawn back into her past when her 'sister' Yelena Belova resurfaces with a chemical weapon that can free Black Widow operatives from their mind control. The two team up with their former 'family' — the super-soldier Alexei and spy Melina — to take down the Red Room and its leader, Dreykov, freeing dozens of brainwashed assassins and giving Yelena a version of Natasha's own escape from that life.
deepDive.significance: The only real look at Natasha's backstory before her death in Endgame, and it hands her legacy directly to Yelena, who becomes an ongoing character across Hawkeye and beyond.
deepDive.orderNote: Set in 2016, directly after Civil War, so it's grouped here narratively rather than by its actual 2021 release.

watchFor.name: Yelena Belova
watchFor.thisFilm: Reunites with her 'sister' Natasha and helps take down the Red Room.
watchFor.future: Becomes the next Black Widow, continuing the legacy through Hawkeye and beyond.

watchFor.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: A mysterious government operative approaches Yelena at Natasha's grave.
watchFor.future: Later revealed to be assembling her own team of antiheroes across Phase Four and Five.

postCredit.skipNote: Skip this movie's credit scene if you're following narrative order. It's set after her Endgame, which you haven't watched yet at this point. Come back and watch it right before Hawkeye, S1 Disney+.

movies.title: Black Panther
movies.summary: After his father's death, T'Challa returns to the technologically advanced nation of Wakanda to claim the throne, but a challenger with ties to his family's past threatens both his crown and Wakanda's secrets.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up only days after the last film, with T'Challa heading home to take the throne after events there. Wakanda gets built from the ground up for you — nothing about it is assumed — but the reason he's returning home, and grieving, comes straight out of the previous film.

movies.timeSkip: Set only days after Civil War, though released two years later

deepDive.plot: Following his father's death in Civil War, T'Challa returns to Wakanda to be crowned king, only to be challenged for the throne by Erik Killmonger, an estranged cousin raised in America who was abandoned by Wakanda after his own father's death decades earlier. Killmonger briefly seizes the throne and plans to arm oppressed people worldwide with Wakandan weapons, forcing T'Challa to reclaim his birthright and choose a new path of engaging with the world rather than hiding from it.
deepDive.significance: Fundamentally redefines Wakanda's role in the world (opening it up globally) and introduces Shuri, Okoye, and Killmonger — one of the MCU's most acclaimed villains.
deepDive.orderNote: Set only days after Civil War, so it's placed right behind it even though it released two years later.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Not present in the main story — referenced by Shuri near the end.
watchFor.future: Revealed alive and recovering in Wakanda under the name 'White Wolf,' ahead of Infinity War.

watchFor.name: Wakanda opens to the world
watchFor.thisFilm: T'Challa reveals Wakanda's true technological nature to the United Nations.
watchFor.future: Shapes Wakanda's global role for the rest of the saga.

watchFor.name: Shuri
watchFor.thisFilm: Established as Wakanda's chief technological genius.
watchFor.future: Becomes central to Wakanda's future, especially after Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
movies.summary: Still adjusting to his new abilities, Peter Parker balances high school life with his growing responsibilities as Spider-Man while facing a black-market arms dealer wielding stolen alien technology.

beforeWatch.context: A few months after the airport fight, told from the point of view of the fifteen-year-old who was briefly flown in for it and then sent home. This is a high-school film first and a superhero film second. You need the previous film for how he got the suit, and very little else.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after Civil War

deepDive.plot: Still buzzing from the Avengers' Berlin airport battle, Peter Parker juggles high school with amateur superheroics, eager for Tony Stark to call him up for real missions. When he stumbles onto a black-market arms operation run by Adrian Toomes (the Vulture), selling weapons built from salvaged Chitauri and Avengers-battle technology, Peter's over-eagerness nearly gets people killed, forcing him to learn responsibility the hard way before defeating Toomes without Iron Man's help.
deepDive.significance: Reboots Spider-Man within the MCU's own continuity, deepens Peter's mentor/mentee relationship with Tony, and plants a 'salvaged alien tech' black market that recurs in later Spider-Man films.
deepDive.orderNote: Set a couple of months after Civil War, continuing straight from Peter's MCU debut there.

watchFor.name: Adrian Toomes / Vulture
watchFor.thisFilm: Defeated and imprisoned, but refuses to reveal Spider-Man's identity to a fellow inmate.
watchFor.future: Kept alive rather than killed off, leaving the door open for a larger criminal threat later.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark's mentorship
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony offers Peter a spot on the Avengers, which Peter turns down.
watchFor.future: Deepens Peter's ties to the Avengers, paying off emotionally in Infinity War and Endgame.

movies.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
movies.summary: Scott Lang juggles house arrest with a new mission alongside Hope van Dyne and Hank Pym to rescue Hope's mother, Janet, from the mysterious and dangerous Quantum Realm.

beforeWatch.context: Scott is under house arrest for taking part in the airport fight, and the film is a light, self-contained caper — a deliberate breather. Important placement note: it runs alongside the previous film rather than after it, and only catches up to that film's ending in its final moments.

movies.timeSkip: Set concurrently with, right up to, Infinity War's ending

deepDive.plot: Still under house arrest after Civil War, Scott Lang is pulled back into Hank Pym and Hope van Dyne's world when they need his unique Quantum Realm experience to rescue Hope's mother, Janet, who's been trapped there for three decades. Their efforts to build a working tunnel into the Quantum Realm are complicated by a black-market tech dealer and a mysterious, phasing woman named Ghost, who needs Janet's quantum energy to stabilize her own condition. They successfully retrieve Janet just as the Snap disintegrates half the universe outside — including Hope, Hank, and Janet — leaving Scott alone and stranded in the Quantum Realm.
deepDive.significance: Introduces the Quantum Realm mechanics in enough depth that it becomes the literal basis for the time-travel plan in Endgame, and its ending directly explains Scott's mysterious absence at the start of that film.
deepDive.orderNote: Set concurrently with Infinity War's climax, explaining what the Ant-Man family was doing while the Snap happened elsewhere.

watchFor.name: The Quantum Realm
watchFor.thisFilm: Explored in depth as Hank and Hope search for Janet.
watchFor.future: Becomes the mechanism the team uses for time travel in Avengers: Endgame.

watchFor.name: Janet van Dyne's rescue
watchFor.thisFilm: Successfully rescued after 30 years trapped in the Quantum Realm.
watchFor.future: Brings her decades of Quantum Realm knowledge into the eventual fight against Thanos.

watchFor.name: The credits-scene Snap
watchFor.thisFilm: Scott Lang is left stranded in the Quantum Realm when his team outside disintegrates.
watchFor.future: Explains his absence at the very start of Endgame.

postCredit.timing: The mid-credit scene plays fairly early; the real post-credit scene (Scott stranded and alone) doesn't hit until after the full cast and crew crawl, so it's easy to miss if you stop early.
postCredit.skipNote: Skip both credit scenes if you're following the narative order! Come back after Infinity War.

movies.title: Thor: Ragnarok
movies.summary: Imprisoned on the other side of the universe, Thor must race home to stop the fire demon Surtur and his ruthless sister Hela from destroying Asgard, teaming up with the Hulk and a band of misfits along the way.

beforeWatch.context: Thor has spent two years off-screen chasing the thread he walked away on at the end of Age of Ultron, and comes back to find things at home very different. A hard tonal swerve into comedy compared with the previous two — that's deliberate. Both earlier Thor films and Age of Ultron feed directly into where he is when it opens.

deepDive.plot: Imprisoned across the universe by the Grandmaster on the trash-planet Sakaar, Thor must escape and race home after learning his long-hidden older sister, Hela, the Goddess of Death, has seized Asgard's throne and set her sights on galactic conquest. Reluctantly teaming up with an exiled Valkyrie, a captive Hulk, and a scheming Loki, Thor allows the fire demon Surtur to destroy Asgard entirely rather than let Hela keep it, saving his people — now refugees — at the cost of his home.
deepDive.significance: A tonal reinvention of the Thor franchise that nonetheless ends in real tragedy, the loss of Asgard, and directly sets up Thanos's attack at the very start of Infinity War.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the last calm-before-the-storm story before Infinity War, with its ending flowing directly into that film's opening scene.

watchFor.name: The refugee ship (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Thor leads Asgard's survivors away from their destroyed home on a massive ship.
watchFor.future: Intercepted by an ominous, much larger vessel — the opening moment of Avengers: Infinity War.

watchFor.name: Asgard's destruction
watchFor.thisFilm: Thor allows Surtur to destroy Asgard in order to defeat Hela.
watchFor.future: Leaves Thor without a kingdom or home, shaping his arc through Endgame.

watchFor.name: Valkyrie
watchFor.thisFilm: Gives up drinking and rejoins the fight to save Asgard's people.
watchFor.future: Becomes the leader of the Asgardian refugees, continuing into New Asgard and Love and Thunder.

movies.title: Avengers: Infinity War
movies.summary: The Avengers and their allies unite to stop the Mad Titan Thanos from collecting all six Infinity Stones and using them to wipe out half of all life in the universe.

beforeWatch.context: This is the film that every film so far has been leading up to. This movie moves between Earth and deep space constantly, and expects you to already know the cosmic crew, the state of Wakanda, where the team stands after Civil War, and what the various coloured stones people keep chasing actually are. Keep a mental tally of the stones we already know about: Space Stone (Tesseract): Last seen on Asgard - Mind Stone: On Earth, embedded in Vision's forehead - Time Stone (Eye of Agamotto): Around Strange's neck in New York - Reality Stone (Aether): Left with the Collector on Knowhere - Power Stone: Locked away on Xandar in a Nova Corps vault - Soul Stone: No one knows its location.

movies.timeSkip: Directly after the mid-credit scene of Thor: Ragnarok

deepDive.plot: Thanos, having gathered several Infinity Stones already, launches an assault across the galaxy to collect the rest, including the Mind Stone from Vision's forehead and the Time Stone from Doctor Strange, so he can snap away half of all life in the universe to 'balance' it. Despite the combined efforts of nearly every hero introduced across a decade of films, Thanos succeeds, and the film ends with half of all life, including many beloved heroes, disintegrating into dust.
deepDive.significance: The culmination of the entire Infinity Saga's setup — every Infinity Stone thread from every prior film pays off here, and its devastating ending redefines the stakes for the rest of the franchise.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed near the end of Phase Three as the direct payoff of a decade of Infinity Stone setups across nearly every prior film.

watchFor.name: The Snap
watchFor.thisFilm: Thanos wipes out half of all life in the universe with a snap of his fingers.

watchFor.name: Avengers' team dynamic post Civil War
Nick Fury's pager (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Fury sends a distress signal moments before disintegrating.
watchFor.future: The page reaches Captain Marvel, who arrives to help in Endgame.

watchFor.name: Gamora's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Sacrificed by Thanos on Vormir to obtain the Soul Stone.
watchFor.future: After the death of Gamora, and the new Gamora takes her place, Peter Quill is left in a state of denial and grief.

watchFor.name: Loki's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Loki officially dies at the hands of Thanos, trying to save his brother and the Space Stone.

postCredit.skipNote: Make sure to go back and watch the Ant-Man and the Wasp post-credit scene after this movie if you're following the narrative order, as it takes place after the events of Infinity War.

movies.title: Captain Marvel
movies.summary: The story follows Vers as she transforms into one of the most powerful heroes in the universe. When a huge space war between two alien groups ends up coming to Earth, she and a small group of friends find themselves trapped right in the middle of the chaos.

beforeWatch.context: Set in 1995, half a century after the WWII film and over a decade before the present day story starts. Watch for younger versions of Fury and Coulson. This takes place long before they became high-ranking S.H.I.E.L.D. figures we know from The Avengers.

deepDive.plot: Set in the mid-1990s, an amnesiac Kree soldier named Vers discovers she's actually Carol Danvers, a former U.S. Air Force pilot who gained cosmic powers from an alien energy core. Along the way she uncovers that the 'enemy' Skrulls she's been hunting are actually refugees, and that her own Kree allies have been lying to her for years. She helps the Skrulls find a new home and leaves Earth to help them resettle across the galaxy.
deepDive.significance: Introduces one of the MCU's most powerful heroes and recontextualizes Nick Fury's early career. It stands almost entirely on its own. What it's quietly doing is filling in the era before any of the heroes existed, back when the organisation that eventually assembles them was a much smaller outfit. It seeds two long-term threads: the Tesseract's origins and the Skrulls' true nature, both of which pay off years later. The mid-credits scene jumps straight from 1995 into the immediate aftermath of Infinity War, showing the remaining Avengers gathered around the pager Fury sent. It's also revealed that the Avengers' name was inspired by Carol's Air Force call sign, 'Avenger.'
deepDive.orderNote: Chronologically this film could be placed after Captain America: The First Avenger, but narratively this is the best place to have it. This film matches the intergalactic setting the surrounding films have, rather than placing it right after a more grounded WWII movie. This film also sets up the pager that Nick Fury uses to call Captain Marvel in Endgame, so it makes sense to place it right before Endgame.

watchFor.name: Tesseract
watchFor.thisFilm: The last time we saw it chronologically was in Captain America: The First Avenger, when it fell into the ocean. At the end of the film we see Goose regurgitate it explaining how S.H.I.E.L.D. has it in The Avengers.

watchFor.name: The Skrulls
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduce the Skrulls as a distinct alien race with their own culture and motivations. They're not conquerors, but are actually refugees fleeing Kree genocide.
watchFor.future: Sets up the Skrull-Kree conflict that will play out in later films.

watchFor.name: Ronan the Accuser's Rank
watchFor.thisFilm: When we met him in Guardians of the Galaxy, he was a rogue Kree extremist. In this movie, he is still an official high-ranking military leader.

watchFor.name: Planet Hala
watchFor.future: The planet Hala later shows up as an important location in The Marvels.

watchFor.name: The Supreme Intelligence
watchFor.future: Carol Danvers later returns to Hala to destroy the Supreme Intelligence which sparks the Kree Civil War.

watchFor.name: Maria Rambeau
watchFor.future: Carol's best friend, whose inclusion here is a setup for the broader multiverse as alternative versions of Maria appear later in the series.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness/The Marvels

watchFor.name: Monica Rambeau
watchFor.thisFilm: First appearance as Maria Rambeau's daughter as a little girl.
watchFor.future: This movie sets up her growing up to get her own cosmic powers in WandaVision and fighting alongside Carol as an adult in The Marvels.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury's eye
watchFor.thisFilm: Scratched by Goose the Flerken aboard a Skrull ship. A dissapointit sight

watchFor.name: Talos
watchFor.thisFilm: Reveals himself as a Skrull leader seeking peace, not conquest. Is promised at the end of the film by Nick that he will find a new home for the Skrulls.
watchFor.future: Becomes a recurring ally, and is later revealed to have spent years impersonating Nick Fury and becomes an important character in the D+ series Secret Invasion.

watchFor.name: Goose the Flerken
watchFor.thisFilm: A cat-like alien with tentacles and a pocket dimension in its stomach. Goose is a Flerken, an alien species that looks like cats but has dangerous abilities and a recurring presence in the MCU.

movies.title: Avengers: Endgame
movies.summary: With half of all life gone, the remaining Avengers assemble one final time to undo Thanos's actions, launching a desperate heist through their own history.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up in the immediate aftermath of the Snap, with the survivors in pieces. It runs three hours and it leans on recognition harder than anything else in the run, so the more of the Infinity Saga you still have fresh, the more it hands back to you. The pager Fury sent as he was dusted gets answered here, which is why Captain Marvel sits directly in front of it. Worth having straight going in, who is still standing: Tony and Nebula are stranded in space on Titan, and back on Earth it's Steve, Natasha, Thor, Bruce, Clint, Rhodey, Rocket and Okoye.

movies.timeSkip: Jumps forward 5 years partway through the film, from 2018 to 2023

deepDive.plot: Three weeks after the Snap, the surviving Avengers track down and kill Thanos, only to discover he's already destroyed the Infinity Stones, making his actions permanent. Five years later, Scott Lang's escape from the Quantum Realm reveals the possibility of time travel, and the remaining Avengers stage a 'time heist' across several past MCU films to collect past versions of the Stones and undo the Snap. Reversing the Snap brings back everyone who was dusted, but draws past-Thanos into the present for one final battle, which Tony Stark wins at the cost of his own life.
deepDive.significance: Closes out the Infinity Saga, eleven years and twenty-two films. Every original Avenger either dies, retires or hands their job to someone else here, which is why so much of Phase Four is about people stepping into roles that used to belong to somebody more famous. It also sets the rules the rest of the MCU runs on: the way this film handles time travel, and what the Ancient One says about what happens when you remove a stone from its timeline, is the foundation the Loki series and everything multiverse-related is built on.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits at the end of Phase Three because it answers Infinity War directly. Captain Marvel goes in front of it rather than back in the 1990s where it actually takes place, so that the pager Fury sends at the end of Infinity War gets answered by someone you've already met.

watchFor.name: How the world handled five years of loss
Professor Hulk
watchFor.thisFilm: Bruce turns up already merged with the Hulk, Banner's head on the Hulk's body. The film skips past how he got there and never goes back to it.

watchFor.name: Thor's grief
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes the five years badly. The film plays a lot of it for laughs, which people still argue about.
watchFor.future: Love and Thunder picks him up partway through working it out.

watchFor.name: The Ancient One's rules
watchFor.thisFilm: Explains to Bruce that pulling a stone out of its own time doesn't rewrite history, it splits off a new branch that keeps running.
watchFor.future: That one conversation is the whole basis for the TVA and every multiverse story that follows.

watchFor.name: Cassie Lang
watchFor.thisFilm: Five years older than Scott left her, which is the film's clearest measure of what the gap cost.
watchFor.future: Grown up and building her own suit by Quantumania.

watchFor.name: New Asgard
watchFor.thisFilm: Thor hands the throne to Valkyrie and leaves with the Guardians.
watchFor.future: Love and Thunder opens with both of those still true.

watchFor.name: Black Widow's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Dies on Vormir, trading herself for the Soul Stone after she and Clint each try to be the one who goes.
watchFor.future: Her death is what the Hawkeye series is reacting to, and what Yelena is still angry about years later.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes the stones off Thanos and uses them himself, and it kills him.
watchFor.future: Peter Parker spends two films out from under his shadow, and half of Phase Four is people arguing over what he left behind.

watchFor.name: Steve Rogers' choice
watchFor.thisFilm: Goes back to return the stones and stays there, living the life he missed with Peggy.
watchFor.future: The shield goes to Sam, which is where The Falcon and the Winter Soldier starts.
watchFor.spoils: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier/Brave New World

watchFor.name: The 2012 Loki
watchFor.thisFilm: The heist goes wrong in 2012 and that version of Loki grabs the Tesseract and vanishes.
watchFor.future: That's the Loki the TVA arrests in the first minutes of his series. He's a different person from the one who died in Infinity War, and the series never pretends otherwise.

watchFor.name: The 2014 Gamora
watchFor.thisFilm: A Gamora from before she ever met the Guardians is pulled into the present and walks off on her own.
watchFor.future: She's the Gamora in Vol. 3, and she doesn't remember Quill at all.

movies.title: WandaVision
movies.summary: Grieving in secret, Wanda Maximoff builds an idyllic sitcom life with a resurrected Vision in the town of Westview, a reality that starts to crack the deeper you look.

beforeWatch.context: A few weeks after Endgame. Wanda has lost more than almost anyone across the last two Avengers films and has had no space to process any of it. The series is formally strange. It opens as a black-and-white sitcom and stays in that register for a while, and it is doing that on purpose. Both Avengers films are essential here; the sitcom pastiche is a bonus, not a requirement.

deepDive.plot: Grieving Vision's death and unable to process her trauma from Thanos's Snap, Wanda Maximoff unknowingly seizes control of a small town, Westview, warping reality into a series of decades-spanning sitcom pastiches with a resurrected version of Vision built from her own grief and power. As S.W.O.R.D. investigates the anomaly from outside, the show reveals that Wanda's neighbor Agatha Harkness has secretly been manipulating events to steal Wanda's uniquely powerful magic. Wanda ultimately defeats Agatha, but has to say goodbye to the family she conjured, releasing the townspeople and leaving with the Darkhold to study her own powers in isolation.
deepDive.significance: The first Disney+ series, and the show that turns Wanda from an Avenger who has lost people into the Scarlet Witch. It's also the first time the MCU spends nine episodes on one person's grief instead of a fight, and the ending sets up almost everything Wanda does afterwards.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed first in Phase Four as the earliest post-Endgame story chronologically, unfolding just months after the Blip is reversed.

watchFor.name: Monica Rambeau
watchFor.thisFilm: The girl from Captain Marvel, grown up and working for S.W.O.R.D. She was dusted, came back to find her mother had died during the five years she missed, and crosses the barrier twice.
watchFor.future: Those crossings are what give her powers, which she's still working out how to use in The Marvels.

watchFor.name: Jimmy Woo
watchFor.thisFilm: The FBI agent from Ant-Man and the Wasp, here as the only person outside Westview treating any of it seriously.

watchFor.name: Darcy Lewis
watchFor.thisFilm: Jane Foster's intern from the Thor films, turning up with an actual doctorate and doing most of the useful thinking.

watchFor.name: Agatha Harkness
watchFor.thisFilm: The nosy neighbour, and the one who's been prodding Wanda's grief all season to work out how she does what she does.
watchFor.future: Wanda leaves her locked inside the neighbour persona, which is exactly where Agatha All Along picks her up.

watchFor.name: The Darkhold
watchFor.thisFilm: Agatha's book, which Wanda takes with her at the end and starts reading.
watchFor.future: It's what she's studying when Strange comes looking for her, and it's what turns her into the villain of that film.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

watchFor.name: Wanda's real title
watchFor.thisFilm: Agatha names her. Not a witch with too much power, but the Scarlet Witch of prophecy, a being everyone assumed was a story.
watchFor.future: That name is the entire reason Strange goes looking for her.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

watchFor.name: The twins
watchFor.thisFilm: Wanda has Billy and Tommy inside the Hex, and they go when it does.
watchFor.future: Hearing them call for her is what sends her across the multiverse. Billy turns up again, reincarnated and looking for his brother, in Agatha All Along.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness/Agatha All Along

watchFor.name: The second Vision
watchFor.thisFilm: S.W.O.R.D. rebuilds the real body, white and blank. The two Visions talk each other to a standstill instead of fighting, and the rebuilt one leaves with his memories back and no idea what to do with them.
watchFor.future: Nothing picks that thread up until VisionQuest.
