watchFor.future: Directly leads into her villainous turn in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

movies.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
movies.summary: With Steve Rogers gone, Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes are forced to work together against a group of anti-nationalist super soldiers, while a new government-appointed Captain America stirs controversy.

beforeWatch.context: Around six months after Endgame, following the two men Steve left behind and the question of what happens to the shield now. The world is dealing with the practical mess of half the population returning after five years away. The Winter Soldier is the key film to have fresh, since this series carries straight on from that story's politics.

movies.timeSkip: Roughly six months after the Blip is reversed

deepDive.plot: With Steve Rogers retired, Sam Wilson struggles with the weight of the shield he was given, ultimately donating it to a museum, while the government hands the Captain America mantle to a decorated but volatile soldier, John Walker. Sam and a restless Bucky Barnes reluctantly team up to stop the Flag-Smashers, a group of super-soldiers who believe the world was better during the Blip's more equal chaos. After Walker publicly kills a Flag-Smasher with the shield and is stripped of the title, Sam reclaims the mantle himself, becoming the first Black Captain America and confronting the government about America's history of failing Black soldiers like the forgotten super-soldier Isaiah Bradley.
deepDive.significance: Passes the Captain America identity to Sam Wilson for good, and introduces both U.S. Agent and a returning Zemo, both of whom recur across later Phase Four and Five stories.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows WandaVision as the next chronological post-Blip story, unfolding over the following months.

watchFor.name: Sam Wilson
watchFor.thisFilm: Hands the shield to the government in the first episode because he doesn't think it's his to carry, and spends the rest of the series working out that he was wrong about why.
watchFor.future: He's Captain America from here on, which is where Brave New World starts.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: Out of prison, in court-ordered therapy, working through a list of people he needs to make amends to. The list is the spine of his half of the story.
watchFor.future: Turns up on Yelena's team years later, still trying to be useful to someone.

watchFor.name: Isaiah Bradley
watchFor.thisFilm: A super soldier from the Korean War the country used, jailed and erased. Nothing about him gets resolved, which is the point.
watchFor.future: His grandson Eli is quietly set up, and Isaiah himself matters again in Brave New World.

watchFor.name: John Walker
watchFor.thisFilm: The government's replacement Captain America, who kills a surrendering man in a public square with the shield and is stripped of the title for it.
watchFor.future: Valentina picks him up almost immediately as U.S. Agent, and he's on the team in Thunderbolts*.

watchFor.name: Helmut Zemo
watchFor.thisFilm: Broken out of prison because they need him, useful for exactly as long as it suits him, and handed to the Dora Milaje at the end.
watchFor.future: The Raft doesn't hold him forever.

watchFor.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up unannounced to recruit Walker, gives no straight answer about who she works for, and leaves.
watchFor.future: She's been assembling a team this whole time, which is what Thunderbolts* is.

watchFor.name: Sharon Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: Living in Madripoor since Civil War, abandoned by the people she helped. The last scene reveals she's the Power Broker, and she gets her pardon and her old clearance back anyway.
watchFor.future: Left sitting inside the government with every reason to resent it, and nothing has been done with it yet.

episodes.title: New World Order
episodes.summary: Sam struggles with the weight of Steve's legacy while a new, more radical Captain America is unveiled by the government.

episodes.title: The Star-Spangled Man
episodes.summary: Sam and Bucky reluctantly team up to track down the Flag-Smashers, a group fighting for a borderless world.

episodes.title: Power Broker
episodes.summary: The hunt for the source of the Flag-Smashers' powers leads Sam and Bucky to enlist the unpredictable Baron Zemo.

episodes.title: The Whole World is Watching
episodes.summary: Tensions boil over as John Walker's actions as the new Captain America spiral out of control.

episodes.title: Truth
episodes.summary: Sam confronts the government and Isaiah Bradley, a forgotten Black super-soldier erased from history, about who gets to be a hero.

episodes.title: One World, One People
episodes.summary: Sam claims the mantle of Captain America for the first time, addressing the world directly about what the shield should stand for.

watchFor.name: Sam Wilson becomes Captain America
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes up the shield and the Captain America identity Steve left him at the end of Endgame.
watchFor.future: Continues into Captain America: Brave New World as the new Captain America.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
movies.summary: While on a school trip across Europe, Peter Parker is recruited by Nick Fury to help a mysterious visitor from another dimension battle a string of elemental creatures threatening the world.

beforeWatch.context: A few months after Endgame, and the first film to show what the world actually looks like afterwards: grieving, disoriented, and trying to work out who fills the gap. Peter is on a school trip to Europe and would very much like a holiday. The previous film's ending is essential; so is his own.

movies.timeSkip: Set 8 years after the 2012 Avengers battle, following the 5-year Blip

deepDive.plot: Grieving Tony Stark's death and adjusting to a post-Blip world where their entire class aged five years while they didn't, Peter Parker just wants a normal school trip to Europe, until Nick Fury recruits him to help a mysterious hero named Mysterio battle giant elemental monsters. Mysterio turns out to be a fraud, a former Stark employee using illusion technology to fake a threat and position himself as Tony's successor, and his final act of revenge is publicly outing Peter's secret identity to the world.
deepDive.significance: The first film to show what the world is actually like after everyone came back, and the last one billed as part of the Infinity Saga. It's mostly about Peter being handed Tony's job at sixteen and not wanting it. Then it ends on the cliffhanger that the next film is entirely about.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits after the two Disney+ series because it takes place a few months further on, and because arriving here with Endgame fresh makes the grief in it land properly.

watchFor.name: How the world talks about the Blip
EDITH
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony leaves Peter a pair of glasses wired to Stark defence systems, including a drone array, and the film is largely about a teenager being handed that and not being ready.

watchFor.name: Quentin Beck
watchFor.thisFilm: Presents himself as a hero from another Earth. He's a former Stark employee with a grudge and a very good illusion rig, and the whole crisis is staged.
watchFor.future: His last move is a doctored video naming Peter, which is the entire premise of No Way Home.

watchFor.name: The multiverse pitch
watchFor.thisFilm: Beck's cover story is that he's from another universe. It's a lie here, told before the multiverse is real, and Fury buys it without much resistance.
watchFor.future: By the next film it isn't a lie any more.

watchFor.name: Happy Hogan
watchFor.thisFilm: The last piece of Tony's world still checking in on Peter, and the one who tells him the shoes were never going to fit.

watchFor.name: MJ and Ned
watchFor.thisFilm: MJ works out who he is on her own, well before he tells her. It matters later that she knew first.
watchFor.future: Both of them lose that entirely at the end of No Way Home.

watchFor.name: J. Jonah Jameson
watchFor.thisFilm: The mid-credits hands the doctored footage to a screaming tabloid broadcaster, played by the same actor who played him in the Raimi films twenty years earlier.
watchFor.future: He's still at it in No Way Home.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury & Maria Hill (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: The Fury and Hill who've been running Peter this whole film are Talos and Soren wearing their faces. The real Fury is off-world on a Skrull ship.
watchFor.future: That's the setup Secret Invasion opens from, and it recasts every Fury scene in the film.

movies.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
movies.summary: After his identity is exposed, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange for help, and a spell gone wrong tears open the multiverse, bringing dangerous visitors from other realities into his world.

beforeWatch.context: Peter Parker's identity as Spider-Man was broadcast to the world at the end of the last film, and this one opens directly on that fallout. He's still a high-school senior, and college applications drive the early going more than the heroics do. The other thing worth carrying in is Doctor Strange, so his solo film gives you a sense of what magic can and can't do here.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after Far From Home

deepDive.plot: With his identity publicly exposed and his loved ones' lives upended, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange to cast a spell making the world forget he's Spider-Man, but Peter's own hesitations corrupt the spell, tearing open the multiverse and pulling in villains, and eventually the Spider-Men themselves, from other Spider-Man universes entirely. After a version of Peter's Aunt May is killed trying to save one of the villains, Peter chooses to help redeem all of them rather than send them back to certain death, at the cost of having Strange erase the entire world's memory of him, which leaves Peter with nothing and no one who knows him.
deepDive.significance: The film that made the multiverse real to people on Earth rather than to the TVA, and the one that finally strips Peter back to a Spider-Man with no money, no mentor and nobody who knows him. It also settles twenty years of Sony continuity by treating the older films as real rather than as a joke.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the direct continuation of Far From Home's ending, unfolding a few months later.

watchFor.name: Peter causes all of this himself
Doctor Strange
watchFor.thisFilm: Agrees to cast a memory spell as a favour, lets Peter talk over him while he's casting it, and spends the rest of the film cleaning up. He's noticeably worse at saying no than he was in his own film.

watchFor.name: Multiversal visitors
watchFor.thisFilm: The broken spell pulls in people who knew Peter Parker was Spider-Man in their own universes, which is why it drags in villains from the Raimi and Webb films rather than random ones. The rule is tighter than it first looks.
watchFor.future: First hard proof the multiverse is real to people on Earth, and Strange spends his next film dealing with the consequences.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

watchFor.name: Norman Osborn
watchFor.thisFilm: The film's actual antagonist, and the one who forces the turn. Willem Dafoe plays him as genuinely split rather than as a callback.

watchFor.name: Curing them instead of sending them back
watchFor.thisFilm: May's argument, and the thing that separates this Peter from the other two. It also gets her killed.

watchFor.name: May Parker
watchFor.thisFilm: Dies at Osborn's hands, and the with-great-power line lands here for the first time in this trilogy because it's her saying it.

watchFor.name: The other two
watchFor.thisFilm: Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield turn up as their own Peters. Garfield catching MJ is the film's best single moment, and both of them are given something to resolve rather than just cameos.

watchFor.name: What the last spell costs
watchFor.thisFilm: Strange erases Peter Parker from everyone's memory to close the multiverse. Not just his identity. Him. MJ and Ned don't know he exists, and he chooses not to tell them.
watchFor.future: He ends the film broke, alone, in a bedsit, sewing his own suit with no Stark tech and no Avengers connections. Brand New Day starts from there.

watchFor.name: Eddie Brock (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Blips out of the bar mid-sentence and leaves a piece of the symbiote behind on the counter.
watchFor.future: The only thing from that universe left in this one, and it hasn't been picked up yet.

movies.title: Hawkeye
movies.summary: Clint Barton teams up with young archer Kate Bishop to take down a criminal conspiracy tied to his past as Ronin, just days before Christmas.

beforeWatch.context: Christmas in New York, with Clint trying and failing to get home to his family. It leans on his history more than any other series, specifically the five years covered by Endgame and the partnership at the heart of Black Widow. A cheerful, low-stakes holiday tone sitting on top of some genuinely heavy history.

deepDive.plot: Trying to get home to his family for Christmas, retired Avenger Clint Barton is dragged back into his past as the vigilante Ronin when aspiring young archer Kate Bishop accidentally puts on his old suit at an auction, drawing the attention of a tracksuit-wearing mafia and Yelena Belova, who blames Clint for Natasha's death. Clint and Kate team up, uncovering that the real villain is a mob boss connected to Kate's own family, and Clint clears his name with Yelena while passing his archer's mantle informally to Kate.
deepDive.significance: Hands the name to Kate Bishop, and gives Clint the only real reckoning anyone has with what the five years after the Snap actually did to people. It also brings Kingpin back from the Netflix shows, which is where that whole corner of the MCU restarts.
deepDive.orderNote: Set at Christmas 2024, placed here as the next confirmed dated story after Loki's 'outside time' events.

watchFor.name: Clint just wants to get home for Christmas
Kate Bishop
watchFor.thisFilm: Twenty-two, extremely good, and completely unprepared for what the job actually involves. She saw Clint fight in New York as a child and has been aiming at this ever since.
watchFor.future: Ends the series with the name, and she's one of the Young Avengers the MCU keeps quietly assembling.

watchFor.name: The Ronin years
watchFor.thisFilm: The five years Clint spent killing people after the Snap. He's not proud of it, the suit resurfaces, and the series is largely about him being made to account for it.
watchFor.future: It's what Yelena and Maya are both here about.

watchFor.name: Yelena Belova
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up hunting Clint because Valentina told her he killed Natasha. The rooftop conversation where she finds out otherwise is the best scene in the show.
watchFor.future: She's on Valentina's team by Thunderbolts*, still carrying this.

watchFor.name: Maya Lopez
watchFor.thisFilm: Deaf, reading lips, running the Tracksuit Mafia and after Ronin for killing her father. Her uncle turns out to be the man who ordered it.
watchFor.future: Walks away from all of it, which is where Echo starts.

watchFor.name: Eleanor Bishop
watchFor.thisFilm: Kate's mother, and the person paying Ronin's old employers. The series makes you like her for five episodes first.

watchFor.name: Laura Barton
watchFor.thisFilm: Clint's wife, who identifies a Rolex by its lot number and turns out to have been an agent long before she was a farmhouse. Watch her, not the watch.

watchFor.name: Kingpin
watchFor.thisFilm: Maya's uncle and the man behind the Tracksuits, brought back for the first time since the Netflix run. Maya shoots him and the show leaves it there.
watchFor.future: He's alive, and both Echo and Daredevil pick him up.

episodes.title: Never Meet Your Heroes
episodes.summary: Kate Bishop accidentally puts on a mysterious Ronin suit at an auction, drawing Clint Barton back into a world he'd hoped to leave behind.

episodes.title: Hide and Seek
episodes.summary: Clint and Kate try to track down the tracksuit-wearing gang hunting the Ronin suit before Christmas gets any more complicated.

episodes.title: Echoes
episodes.summary: The pair run into Maya Lopez, a deaf crime-family enforcer with her own grudge against Ronin.

episodes.title: Partners, Am I Right?
episodes.summary: A captured Clint and Kate must talk their way out of trouble while Yelena Belova closes in on Clint.

episodes.title: Ronin
episodes.summary: Flashbacks reveal what really happened during Clint's brutal Ronin rampage during the Blip.

episodes.title: So This Is Christmas?
episodes.summary: Clint and Kate team up to take down the head of the criminal conspiracy once and for all, on Christmas Eve.

movies.title: Loki: Season 1
movies.summary: After stealing the Tesseract during the Avengers' 2012 time heist, a variant of the God of Mischief is arrested by the Time Variance Authority and forced to help hunt an even more dangerous variant of himself.

beforeWatch.context: This is not the Loki you last saw. It follows the 2012 version, picked up at the exact moment he escapes with the Tesseract during the time heist, so none of his later development has happened yet. You need The Avengers for who he was, and Endgame for the scene he escapes from. After that it leaves the timeline almost immediately.

movies.timeSkip: Kicks off the instant 2012-Loki escapes with the Tesseract during Endgame's heist, then unfolds 'outside' the main timeline at the TVA

deepDive.plot: A variant of Loki, plucked from 2012 the instant he escapes with the Tesseract during the Avengers' time heist, is arrested by the Time Variance Authority for deviating from the 'Sacred Timeline.' Given the choice between erasure and helping the TVA hunt a far more dangerous variant of himself, he takes the job, and finds that the fugitive, Sylvie, has a better grasp of the TVA's lies than its own agents do. Their hunt ends at a citadel outside time, where the being who built the whole apparatus offers them his chair, and Sylvie's answer shatters the single timeline into many.
deepDive.significance: Formally opens the multiverse as a story engine, introduces the Kang lineage as the saga's next big-picture threat, and starts the most complete redemption arc any MCU character gets.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Hawkeye since, while it unfolds 'outside time,' it's triggered by the 2012 scene revisited during Endgame's heist and threaded through that same post-Endgame period. Watch it before Quantumania, because that film's villain only lands once you've met the man in the citadel.

watchFor.name: The Time Variance Authority
watchFor.thisFilm: An organisation outside time that prunes any timeline branching off the approved one, staffed by people who believe they were created for the job. They weren't. They're all variants themselves, taken from their own lives and mind-wiped.
watchFor.future: Everything multiverse-shaped in the MCU runs through this idea.

watchFor.name: Which Loki this is
watchFor.thisFilm: The 2012 version who grabbed the Tesseract during the Endgame heist. He hasn't had Thor: The Dark World or Ragnarok. He's still the man from the first Avengers film, and the series makes him earn everything from there.
watchFor.future: Runs straight into season two.

watchFor.name: Mobius
watchFor.thisFilm: The analyst assigned to him, and the first person to treat Loki as someone worth arguing with rather than containing.

watchFor.name: Sylvie
watchFor.thisFilm: A Loki variant taken by the TVA as a child, who has spent her whole life since trying to burn it down. She's the season's other half, not a love interest bolted on.
watchFor.future: Her choice at the end is what season two spends ten hours dealing with.

watchFor.name: The man at the end of time
watchFor.thisFilm: The citadel at the end of the season holds a tired man who set the TVA up to stop his own variants from finding each other. He offers Loki and Sylvie the job, tells them what happens if they refuse, and Sylvie kills him anyway.
watchFor.future: Quantumania introduces one of the variants he was afraid of, and season two is entirely about whether he was telling the truth.
watchFor.spoils: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania/Loki: Season 2

episodes.title: Glorious Purpose
episodes.summary: A 2012 variant of Loki is arrested by the TVA the moment he escapes with the Tesseract, and given an impossible choice to avoid being erased from existence.

episodes.title: The Variant
episodes.summary: Loki is recruited to help TVA agent Mobius hunt a mysterious variant who's been killing Minutemen across the timeline.

episodes.title: Lamentis
episodes.summary: Loki and the variant Sylvie are stranded together on a moon about to be destroyed, forcing an uneasy alliance.

episodes.title: The Nexus Event
episodes.summary: Loki and Sylvie's growing bond causes a branch in the timeline serious enough to draw the TVA's full attention.

watchFor.name: The Void's Loki variants
watchFor.thisFilm: A group of Loki variants exiled to the end of time is glimpsed, including a child version and an alligator.
watchFor.future: Expands on just how many timeline branches and variants of a single character can exist.

episodes.title: Journey Into Mystery
episodes.summary: Loki meets a collection of his own variants exiled to a wasteland at the end of time, guarded by a terrifying creature.

episodes.title: For All Time. Always.
episodes.summary: Loki and Sylvie reach the being secretly controlling the TVA from behind the curtain, and must decide the fate of the entire multiverse.

watchFor.name: He Who Remains
watchFor.thisFilm: Reveals himself as the true architect of the TVA, having ended a war between his own variants by pruning every other timeline.
watchFor.future: His death fractures the Sacred Timeline into a true multiverse, and a variant of him becomes a major villain later.

movies.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
movies.summary: Scott Lang and his family are pulled into the Quantum Realm, where they run headfirst into a powerful being who has been waiting there for a very long time.

beforeWatch.context: Scott has been enjoying the fame he earned in Endgame, and the film opens on him coasting. It then goes somewhere completely different. Most of it takes place in a setting the earlier Ant-Man films only glimpsed. Loki is worth having behind you: the antagonist here is introduced by that series first.

deepDive.plot: Scott Lang, enjoying newfound fame as an Avenger and author, is accidentally pulled into the Quantum Realm along with his daughter Cassie, Hope, Hank, and Janet, after Cassie's own device to map the realm goes wrong. There, they discover Janet has been hiding a dark secret: decades earlier she encountered Kang the Conqueror, a being exiled to the Quantum Realm after being stripped of his empire by his own alternate selves. Kang manipulates the group into repairing his ship so he can escape and resume his conquest of the multiverse, but the family unites the Realm's oppressed population to defeat him instead, though a much larger council of Kang variants is revealed watching from beyond.
deepDive.significance: Formally introduces Kang the Conqueror as the driving villain of the Multiverse Saga, expands the Quantum Realm into a fully realized world of its own, and gives Cassie Lang a much larger heroic role.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Five as the first story to introduce the saga's next big-picture threat.

watchFor.name: Kang the Conqueror
watchFor.thisFilm: Exiled to the Quantum Realm by his own variants and stripped of his ship. He isn't a man who wants to conquer, he's a man who already did it across countless timelines and got outvoted.
watchFor.future: The Council of Kangs in the mid-credits is the point of the whole film.

watchFor.name: Janet van Dyne's thirty years
watchFor.thisFilm: The film finally answers what she was doing down there, and the answer is that she met Kang, helped him, worked out what he was, and stranded him. She's been not telling anyone since.
watchFor.future: It reframes her silence in the previous film.

watchFor.name: Cassie Lang
watchFor.thisFilm: Built her own shrinking tech, has been arrested for protesting, and is far more willing to be a hero than her father would like.
watchFor.future: One of the Young Avengers the MCU keeps setting up without assembling.

watchFor.name: MODOK
watchFor.thisFilm: Darren Cross from the first Ant-Man, rebuilt by Kang into something with a very large head. The film plays him for laughs, which people either loved or hated.

watchFor.name: The Council of Kangs
watchFor.thisFilm: The mid-credits fills an arena with variants of the man Scott just beat, and they're annoyed that he was killed rather than worried about it.
watchFor.future: This was the setup for the next two Avengers films before the casting changed and Doomsday went in a different direction.

watchFor.name: Victor Timely (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: The post-credits drops into 1901, where a nervous inventor is demonstrating impossible machines while Loki and Mobius watch from the back of the room.
watchFor.future: It's a direct trailer for Loki season two.

movies.title: Loki: Season 2
movies.summary: With the timeline shattered and the TVA in disarray, Loki is torn loose in time itself and races to hold the fraying agency together before its machinery, and every branching reality it was built to police, comes apart.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up in the immediate aftermath of season one, so that needs to be fresh. This season assumes you remember exactly who Loki met at the end of it and what Sylvie chose to do. Watch Quantumania first as well: it properly introduces Kang the Conqueror, and this season deals with the wider problem that film sets up. Much more of a workplace ensemble than season one, and considerably more technical.

deepDive.plot: Loki finds himself 'time-slipping', yanked helplessly between past and future versions of the TVA, while the agency reels from what happened at the citadel. As the Temporal Loom that processes the branching timelines strains past its limits, Loki, Mobius and OB chase a nineteenth-century inventor with a very familiar face, hunt a rogue agent, and try every engineering fix available to them. When none of them hold, Loki is left choosing between the version of the multiverse he wanted and the one that survives.
deepDive.significance: Resolves the TVA arc and settles what the multiverse actually is going forward, while turning Loki from a schemer chasing a throne into someone who accepts a purpose with no glory in it at all.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Quantumania because that film introduces Kang the Conqueror properly, and this season is the direct answer to the problem season one's ending created.

watchFor.name: The Temporal Loom
watchFor.thisFilm: The machine the TVA uses to weave branching timelines into one, failing because it was built for a single thread and there are now far too many. Most of the season is an engineering problem.

watchFor.name: Victor Timely
watchFor.thisFilm: A variant of the man from the citadel, working in 1903 from a technical manual Ravonna handed him as a child. He's decent and frightened and nothing like the original, which is the point the season is making about variants.

watchFor.name: Ravonna Renslayer
watchFor.thisFilm: Follows her belief in the TVA all the way down and finds nothing at the bottom of it. Ends the season abandoned in the Void.

watchFor.name: Miss Minutes
watchFor.thisFilm: The cartoon mascot, which was never a mascot. Her loyalty is to the man who built her, and she's been steering things since before the series started.

watchFor.name: Mobius
watchFor.thisFilm: Learns what his life was before the TVA took it, goes to look at it, and doesn't knock on the door.
watchFor.future: Leaves the job at the end.

watchFor.name: What Loki chooses
watchFor.thisFilm: He stops trying to fix the Loom and takes its place instead, holding every branch himself, alone, forever. It's the throne he wanted in the first film, redefined into the loneliest job that exists.
watchFor.future: This is where the multiverse comes from as a working thing rather than a threat, and it's why every branch is allowed to keep running.

episodes.title: Ouroboros
episodes.summary: Loki is scattered through time by 'time-slipping' after the season one finale and must be rescued by Mobius and the TVA's repair technician, OB.

episodes.title: Breaking Brad
episodes.summary: Loki and the team track down a rogue variant impersonating a TV star while the TVA's timeline monitors start to fail.
The hunt for a new variant leads Loki and Mobius to a World's Fair in 19th-century Chicago.

episodes.title: Heart of the TVA
episodes.summary: With the timeline branching out of control, the team races to stabilize the Temporal Loom before it destroys everything.

episodes.title: Science/Fiction
episodes.summary: Loki and Sylvie clash over how far to go to save the timeline, as the multiverse teeters on total collapse.

watchFor.name: Sylvie's choice
watchFor.thisFilm: Chooses to let the multiverse branch freely rather than trust another 'He Who Remains' variant.
watchFor.future: Sets up a multiverse full of unchecked Kang variants as a threat across Phase Five and Six.

episodes.title: Glorious Purpose
episodes.summary: Loki makes the ultimate sacrifice to hold the multiverse's timelines together himself, becoming the silent god at the center of it all.

watchFor.name: Loki as the multiverse's anchor
watchFor.thisFilm: Chooses to wind himself around every timeline, permanently sacrificing his own future to keep the multiverse from collapsing.
watchFor.future: Leaves the fate of the branching multiverse (and Loki himself) as an open question for the rest of the Multiverse Saga.

movies.title: Deadpool & Wolverine
movies.summary: Recruited by the TVA to help save his own universe from being erased, a reluctant Deadpool drags a jaded variant of Wolverine along on a chaotic, foul-mouthed multiversal detour.

beforeWatch.context: Tonally unlike everything else here: it is loud, aggressively crude, and spends much of its runtime making fun of the films you've just watched. What it needs from you is the Loki series, since the organisation that kicks off the plot is introduced there. It also leans hard on two decades of non-MCU X-Men films. None of them are required, but all of them are rewarded.

movies.inUniverseSetting: 2024 (Deadpool's home universe), mostly set in the Void — a place outside time and space

deepDive.plot: Failed Avengers try-out Wade Wilson is recruited by the TVA to help save his own universe from being erased following the death of its 'anchor being', which in his universe was Wolverine. Wade drags an alternate, jaded, and initially reluctant Wolverine variant along on a mission through the Void, the graveyard of pruned timelines, where they encounter a host of characters and actors from the 20th Century Fox X-Men films, and team up to stop a powerful telepath, Cassandra Nova, from taking over the Void and, eventually, the Sacred Timeline itself.
deepDive.significance: Brings the Fox era into the MCU without merging it, by making the Void a place where discarded universes end up. It also lets the MCU acknowledge out loud that it bought a film library, which is the actual subject of the film.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the direct continuation of the TVA and multiverse concepts introduced in Loki, unfolding after that show's two seasons.

watchFor.name: How much of this is about Fox being bought
The TVA, post-Loki
watchFor.thisFilm: Still pruning, still convinced it knows best, now run by an ambitious analyst called Paradox who wants to speed a dying universe along rather than wait it out.
watchFor.future: It's the same organisation from Loki, operating as if that season never happened to it, which is deliberate.

watchFor.name: Anchor beings
watchFor.thisFilm: The film's rule is that some universes are held together by one person, and when that person dies the universe unravels. Wade's anchor was his Logan, and his Logan is dead when the film opens.

watchFor.name: Wade Wilson
watchFor.thisFilm: Failed the Avengers audition years ago, gave up being Deadpool, and sells cars. The whole film is him deciding he's worth something to the people who already know him.

watchFor.name: Logan
watchFor.thisFilm: Not the Logan from the Fox films' ending. A variant who was too late to save his X-Men and has been drinking about it since, wearing the yellow suit for the first time on screen.

watchFor.name: Cassandra Nova
watchFor.thisFilm: Charles Xavier's twin sister, exiled to the Void as a child, running it by the time they arrive. She is by some distance the most frightening thing in the film.

watchFor.name: The Void
watchFor.thisFilm: Where the TVA dumps whatever it prunes, and therefore where every discarded Fox-era character has ended up. That's the joke and the plot at the same time.

watchFor.name: Who turns up in the Void
watchFor.thisFilm: Elektra, Blade, Gambit and X-23 make up the resistance, and the cameos elsewhere run deeper than that. Nothing is explained, which is the right call.

watchFor.name: What actually changes
watchFor.thisFilm: The Fox universe isn't merged into the main one. It's saved and left alone, and Wade goes home. The MCU gains a doorway rather than a roster.
watchFor.future: Which characters walk through it is still open.

movies.title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
movies.summary: A martial-arts prodigy who has been hiding from his past is drawn back into the orbit of his father's secret organization, the Ten Rings, and must confront a fate he thought he'd escaped.

beforeWatch.context: Almost entirely standalone, with a new cast and a story about a family rather than a world-ending threat. It builds its own mythology from scratch. The one thread reaching back is an organisation whose name has come up a couple of times before, notably in the first Iron Man film.

deepDive.plot: Shaun, a San Francisco valet who's secretly Shang-Chi, has spent a decade hiding from his father Xu Wenwu, the immortal leader of the Ten Rings organization and wielder of ten mystical rings. When his father hunts him down seeking a pendant tied to Shang-Chi's late mother's home village, Shang-Chi learns his father plans to break through a mystical seal, believing his dead wife is trapped behind it. It is actually the prison of a soul-devouring creature. Shang-Chi, his sister Xialing, and their allies stop the creature's escape, and Shang-Chi reluctantly accepts his father's rings and legacy.
deepDive.significance: Introduces a major new hero and organization to the MCU with deep ties to earlier films (the Mandarin hoax from Iron Man 3), and its mid-credit scene formally reconnects the Ten Rings to the wider cosmic mysteries the MCU is building toward.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed in the same broad post-Blip 'present day' period as WandaVision and Falcon/Winter Soldier, though its story is self-contained.

watchFor.name: A film that assumes almost nothing
Xu Wenwu
watchFor.thisFilm: The actual Mandarin, a thousand years old, and the film's best argument that a villain works better when you understand him. Grief is doing all of it.

watchFor.name: Trevor Slattery
watchFor.thisFilm: The actor Killian hired to play the Mandarin in Iron Man 3, imprisoned by the real organisation for the insult and kept alive because he's entertaining. The joke from that film gets a proper ending.

watchFor.name: Katy
watchFor.thisFilm: Refuses to be the friend who gets left behind, and the film gives her a real arc rather than a punchline.

watchFor.name: Xialing
watchFor.thisFilm: Built her own fight club after being shut out of her father's training, and takes over the organisation at the end while telling Shang-Chi she's shutting it down.
watchFor.future: That last shot leaves her running a criminal network nobody has followed up on.

watchFor.name: Abomination
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up in the cage fight against Wong, apparently on friendly terms with him. First sight of Blonsky since The Incredible Hulk.
watchFor.future: She-Hulk explains what he's been doing.

watchFor.name: Wong
watchFor.thisFilm: Recruits both Shang-Chi and, seemingly, half the MCU's loose ends. He's quietly become the person who handles anything strange.

watchFor.name: The rings themselves (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Wong, Carol Danvers and Bruce Banner examine them and find they're far older than anyone thought, and that they've started sending a signal to something.
watchFor.future: Still unanswered.

movies.title: Eternals
movies.summary: A team of immortal beings who have secretly protected Earth for thousands of years are forced to reunite against their ancient enemies, the Deviants, uncovering long-hidden truths about their true purpose.

beforeWatch.context: A near-total reset: a new group who have been on Earth for seven thousand years without ever getting involved in anything you've watched, which the film addresses directly. It works cold. It's also the longest and slowest film here, and jumps between the present day and flashbacks across millennia.

deepDive.plot: A team of ten immortal beings, secretly sent to Earth 7,000 years ago by the cosmic being Arishem to protect humanity from monstrous Deviants, reunite in the present day when the Deviants unexpectedly resurface. The team discovers their true purpose was never protection. They were meant to incubate a Celestial embryo inside the Earth itself, an 'Emergence' that would destroy the planet to birth a new Celestial. Split over whether to let it happen, the Eternals stop the Emergence, but Arishem takes several of them away to judge whether humanity deserves to survive, leaving their fate unresolved.
deepDive.significance: Puts the Celestials on screen as the things that made the galaxy work, and answers where Earth came from in a way no other film has touched. It also leaves more unresolved threads than anything else in Phase Four, and almost none have been picked up.
deepDive.orderNote: Grouped with Shang-Chi and other 2021-released stories in the broad post-Blip period, since its 'present day' scenes align with them despite its ancient flashbacks.

watchFor.name: Why they sat out everything else
The Celestials
watchFor.thisFilm: Arishem made the Eternals, sends them to protect developing planets, and wipes their memories between assignments. They aren't gods and they aren't free.

watchFor.name: Sersi
watchFor.thisFilm: Handed the leadership she never wanted, and the film's argument is that caring about individual people is a qualification rather than a weakness.

watchFor.name: Thena and Gilgamesh
watchFor.thisFilm: Millennia of memory doing to Thena what it would do to anyone, and Gilgamesh quietly looking after her for centuries. The best relationship in the film.

watchFor.name: Druig
watchFor.thisFilm: Can control minds and has spent thousands of years being told not to. The film takes his objection seriously rather than treating it as villainy.

watchFor.name: Phastos
watchFor.thisFilm: Gave humanity technology, watched it used on Hiroshima, and stopped. Also the first Eternal to have an ordinary family.

watchFor.name: What Earth actually is
watchFor.thisFilm: A Celestial called Tiamut has been gestating in the planet's core the whole time, and every civilisation the Eternals helped grow was feeding it. The Emergence would hatch it and destroy the world.
watchFor.future: They stop it, and Tiamut's hand is left standing out of the ocean. Nothing has addressed it since.

watchFor.name: Ikaris
watchFor.thisFilm: Knew all of it from the start, killed Ajak to keep it quiet, and flies into the sun when he can't go through with stopping Sersi.

watchFor.name: Arishem's judgment
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes three of them to be judged, and tells Sersi he'll decide whether humanity is worth keeping by looking through her memories.
watchFor.future: Left hanging entirely.

watchFor.name: Eros / Starfox & Pip the Troll (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Turn up aboard their ship offering to help find the three who were taken. Eros introduces himself as Thanos's brother.
watchFor.future: Nothing since.

watchFor.name: Dane Whitman / the Ebony Blade (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Opens a case with his family's cursed sword in it, and an unseen voice asks if he's sure he's ready. The voice is Blade.
watchFor.future: Also nothing since.

movies.title: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
movies.summary: Lawyer Jennifer Walters gains the powers of the Hulk after an accident, and must balance a superhero-law specialty with the messiness of everyday life.

beforeWatch.context: A half-hour legal comedy that is much more sitcom than superhero show, and it knows it. It expects you to know Bruce Banner's history, so The Incredible Hulk and the Avengers films help, as does Shang-Chi for one recurring supporting character. It also breaks the fourth wall constantly, which is the format, not a glitch.

deepDive.plot: After a car accident exposes her to her cousin Bruce Banner's blood, lawyer Jennifer Walters unexpectedly gains her own Hulk form, which she can control far more easily than Bruce ever could, to his visible annoyance. Reluctantly stepping into a superhuman law specialty at her firm, Jennifer navigates dating, online harassment, and a conspiracy to steal her blood, culminating in a fourth-wall-breaking finale where Jennifer literally storms the show's own production to demand a more satisfying ending.
deepDive.significance: Brings Daredevil back properly and picks up The Incredible Hulk fourteen years later, both inside a legal sitcom that spends its finale arguing with its own writers about how MCU shows end.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed near the end of Phase Four in the same 'present day' period as Ms. Marvel and Love and Thunder.

watchFor.name: It is a sitcom, on purpose
Jennifer Walters
watchFor.thisFilm: Gets her powers from Bruce's blood in a car accident and spends the series annoyed that having them is treated as more interesting than being extremely good at her job.

watchFor.name: Emil Blonsky
watchFor.thisFilm: Up for parole, claiming reform, running a wellness retreat for former villains. The seven-limerick apology is real. Whether he's genuine is left deliberately unclear.
watchFor.future: First proper follow-up to The Incredible Hulk in fourteen years.

watchFor.name: Wong
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up constantly, breaks Blonsky out of prison for a sorcerers' duel, and is a terrible witness. He's the connective tissue of this whole stretch of the MCU.

watchFor.name: Matt Murdock
watchFor.thisFilm: Arrives in the yellow suit, wins his case, and leaves in the morning. Played much lighter here than in his own show, which the series knows.
watchFor.future: Daredevil: Born Again picks him up in a very different register.

watchFor.name: Titania
watchFor.thisFilm: An influencer who trademarks the She-Hulk name, which is a more accurate depiction of what would happen than most of the MCU manages.

watchFor.name: The finale
watchFor.thisFilm: Jennifer breaks out of the show, walks across the Disney+ menu, and argues with the writers' room about her own ending. Nothing else in the MCU does this.

watchFor.name: Skaar
watchFor.thisFilm: Bruce returns from Sakaar with a teenage son, introduced in the last minute and given nothing to do.
watchFor.future: Unfollowed so far.

movies.title: Moon Knight
movies.summary: A mild-mannered gift shop worker discovers he shares a body with a mercenary, both serving as the reluctant avatar of an Egyptian moon god.

beforeWatch.context: The most self-contained thing on this list. New character, new corner of the world, no crossovers and no required reading whatsoever. It never once mentions the Avengers. Go in cold; the disorientation in the opening episode is entirely intentional.

deepDive.plot: Mild-mannered gift shop worker Steven Grant discovers he shares a body with Marc Spector, a mercenary secretly serving as the avatar of the Egyptian moon god Khonshu. As the two struggle for control, they're forced to stop a cult leader, Arthur Harrow, from resurrecting the goddess Ammit to judge humanity for crimes it hasn't committed yet. Along the way, a third personality, Jake Lockley, is revealed to exist within the same body, hinting the full truth of Marc's fractured identity is still not fully understood even by himself.
deepDive.significance: Establishes that the Egyptian gods are real and active, and does it in a series that touches nothing else in the MCU. It is the clearest proof that these stories can be told without a single Avenger in them.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as a largely self-contained story with no direct thread into the wider Avengers plotline, grouped by release-era rather than a tight timeline link.

watchFor.name: It connects to nothing, and that's the appeal
Steven Grant
watchFor.thisFilm: A gift-shop worker in London who loses time, wakes up in the wrong places, and ropes his ankle to the bed. The series opens inside his version of events, so you learn what's happening at the same rate he does.

watchFor.name: Marc Spector
watchFor.thisFilm: The mercenary Steven shares a body with, and the one who made the bargain. The show treats dissociative identity disorder as the actual subject rather than a twist.

watchFor.name: Khonshu
watchFor.thisFilm: The Egyptian moon god in Marc's head, demanding punishment and offering power. Not a benevolent patron. The other gods seal him in stone partway through, and his own account of why he chose Marc is worse than Marc's.

watchFor.name: Layla El-Faouly
watchFor.thisFilm: Marc's wife, an archaeologist, and the one person who knew him before any of this. Becomes the Scarlet Scarab as an avatar on her own terms rather than by being cornered into it.

watchFor.name: Arthur Harrow
watchFor.thisFilm: A former avatar of Khonshu who left, and now serves Ammit, who judges people for crimes they haven't committed yet. He's calm and reasonable and completely certain, which is what makes him work.

watchFor.name: The asylum episode
watchFor.thisFilm: Halfway through, the series stops and offers a reading in which none of it is real. It doesn't fully take it back either.

watchFor.name: Jake Lockley
watchFor.thisFilm: A third personality neither of the others knew about, doing the killing Marc refuses to do. The last scene reveals Khonshu kept him as his real avatar the whole time.

movies.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
movies.summary: Doctor Strange journeys into the dangerous and mind-bending multiverse with the help of a young woman who can travel between realities, while a powerful force hunts her for her abilities.

beforeWatch.context: Follows directly from the end of No Way Home, and takes the door that film opened as its starting premise. It also assumes you've finished WandaVision — that series does far more setup for this film than the first Doctor Strange does. A noticeably darker, more horror-inflected film than anything before it.

deepDive.plot: Hunted by a mysterious force after a wedding goes wrong, America Chavez — a young woman who can punch holes between universes — draws Doctor Strange into the multiverse for the first time. They discover the hunter is actually Wanda Maximoff, consumed by the Darkhold and trying to steal America's powers to travel to a universe where she can be reunited with her children. Strange, forced to use dangerously corrupting magic himself to stop her, ultimately convinces Wanda to see what she's become, and she destroys the Darkhold and herself along with it, seemingly ending the Scarlet Witch's story — for now.
deepDive.significance: Pays off Wanda's entire arc from WandaVision in tragic fashion, and formally confirms the multiverse as a huge, story-spanning concept full of alternate versions of familiar heroes.
deepDive.orderNote: Directly follows No Way Home's confirmation of the multiverse, placed right after it.

watchFor.name: Incursions
watchFor.thisFilm: Strange witnesses a universe-ending 'incursion' while multiverse-traveling.
watchFor.future: Sets the stakes for future multiversal threats.

watchFor.name: America Chavez
watchFor.thisFilm: Escapes with Strange after her powers are hunted by Wanda.
watchFor.future: Her ability to travel the multiverse makes her a target again in future stories.

watchFor.name: Clea (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Approaches Strange after the darkness he dabbled in catches up to him.
watchFor.future: Recruits him to fix the incursion he caused, teasing his next adventure.

movies.title: Agatha All Along
movies.summary: Trapped and powerless since the end of WandaVision, Agatha Harkness assembles a coven of misfit witches to help her survive the deadly Witches' Road and reclaim her magic.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up some time after WandaVision, following that show's most memorable supporting character. It's a road-trip story with a witchy, theatrical register all its own. WandaVision is essential; Multiverse of Madness fills in what's happened to magic in the meantime but isn't strictly required.

deepDive.plot: Trapped and stripped of most of her memory and power since the end of WandaVision, Agatha Harkness is freed by a mysterious teenage boy who leads her to a legendary, deadly trial called the Witches' Road, said to grant whoever survives it their heart's greatest desire. Agatha assembles a ragtag coven of witches, each hiding a secret of their own, to walk the Road with her, and as they face trial after trial — losing members along the way — the boy's true identity and Agatha's real, long-hidden motive for seeking the Road are finally revealed.
deepDive.significance: Expands the MCU's magic-focused corner of the universe introduced in WandaVision, giving Agatha Harkness — one of the most acclaimed side characters of Phase Four — her own complete story.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed at the end of Phase Five as a direct continuation of Agatha's arc from WandaVision, set some time after that show's finale.

watchFor.name: The Witches' Road
watchFor.thisFilm: A legendary, dangerous trial said to grant a witch's greatest desire to whoever survives it.
watchFor.future: Its true nature is a mystery the whole season is built around.

watchFor.future: Recontextualizes everything once revealed.

movies.title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
movies.summary: Following the loss of their king, the people of Wakanda must fight to protect their nation from intervening world powers while facing a new threat from a hidden underwater civilization.

beforeWatch.context: About a year after Endgame, and about a year after the death of T'Challa — which the film treats as real and permanent, and which is also the real-world reason for its shape. It is first and last a film about grief. The first Black Panther is essential; Wakanda's new position in the world follows on directly from it.

movies.timeSkip: Roughly a year after T'Challa's death

deepDive.plot: Following King T'Challa's death from an unspecified illness, Wakanda must defend itself from world powers seeking vibranium, while a hidden underwater civilization called Talokan, led by the mutant king Namor, declares war after Wakanda is blamed for exposing his people's existence. Shuri, consumed by grief and anger, briefly embraces the Black Panther mantle's power for vengeance, but ultimately chooses mercy over Namor's death, forging an uneasy peace between the two nations instead.
deepDive.significance: Passes the Black Panther mantle to Shuri, introduces Namor and Talokan as a major new nation and faction, and reveals T'Challa's secret son Toussaint as a future heir to Wakanda's legacy.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed at the end of Phase Four as the culmination of Wakanda's post-T'Challa arc, roughly a year after his death.

watchFor.name: Namor & Talokan
watchFor.thisFilm: Wages war on the surface world before reaching an uneasy truce with Wakanda.
watchFor.future: Leaves room for future conflict or alliance.

watchFor.name: Shuri as Black Panther
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes up her brother's mantle to defend Wakanda.
watchFor.future: Shapes Wakanda's future direction.

watchFor.name: Toussaint / T'Challa's son (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Not present in the main story — revealed only in the post-credit scene.

movies.title: Thor: Love and Thunder
movies.summary: Thor's search for inner peace is interrupted by a galactic killer known as Gorr the God Butcher, who seeks the extinction of the gods, forcing Thor to seek help from an old flame wielding his own hammer.

beforeWatch.context: Thor has been off with the Guardians since Endgame and is looking for a purpose. Ragnarok's comic register is dialled up further here. The two films that matter going in are Ragnarok, for the tone and the supporting cast, and Endgame, for where he ended up — plus a memory of Jane Foster from the first two Thor films.

deepDive.plot: Still searching for peace after Endgame, Thor reunites with his ex, astrophysicist Jane Foster, who has used the remains of his old hammer Mjolnir to become the Mighty Thor while secretly battling cancer. Together they must stop Gorr the God Butcher, a grief-stricken former believer slaughtering gods across the universe after his own deity abandoned him, using a weapon capable of killing gods, the Necrosword. Jane sacrifices herself using Mjolnir's power to save the day, and Thor, having lost yet another partner, finds a new sense of purpose raising Gorr's resurrected daughter as his own.
deepDive.significance: Gives Jane Foster a definitive, if bittersweet, send-off as the Mighty Thor, and continues Thor's long arc of loss and reinvention that began all the way back in Phase One.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here in the same broad post-Blip period as Ms. Marvel and She-Hulk.

watchFor.name: Jane Foster / Mighty Thor's fate
watchFor.thisFilm: Sacrifices herself using Mjolnir to save Thor and the children of Asgard.
watchFor.future: Her journey to Valhalla leaves the door open for a possible future return.

watchFor.name: Hercules (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Not present in the main story.

movies.title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
movies.summary: While the Guardians spend the holidays quietly grieving and reminiscing on Knowhere, Mantis and Drax journey to Earth on an ill-advised mission to get Peter Quill the perfect Christmas gift: Kevin Bacon.

beforeWatch.context: A forty-minute comedy, set at Christmas, that exists to give the crew a light moment before their final film. It assumes you know where everyone stands after Endgame and Vol. 2 — particularly who is and isn't on the ship any more. There is no threat and no plot to speak of, which is the point.

movies.timeSkip: A few months before Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3

deepDive.plot: While the rest of the Guardians settle into their new home on Knowhere, still grieving a version of Gamora who doesn't remember loving any of them, Mantis and Drax set off on a chaotic mission to Earth to find Peter Quill the perfect Christmas gift after learning how much he misses the holiday traditions of his childhood. Their well-meaning but destructive attempt to 'borrow' actor Kevin Bacon as a present goes about as well as expected, but it gives the grieving team a much-needed dose of levity and connection before their final adventure together.
deepDive.significance: A small-scale, character-focused breather between Vol. 2 and Vol. 3 that quietly confirms Mantis is Star-Lord's half-sister and shows the team's fractured state heading into the final Guardians film.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed at the very end of Phase Four, set just months before Vol. 3's story begins.

watchFor.name: Mantis is Peter Quill's half-sister

watchFor.future: Recontextualizes Mantis and Peter's relationship heading into Vol. 3.

watchFor.name: The team without Gamora

watchFor.future: Sets up the team's fractured dynamic at the start of Vol. 3.

movies.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
movies.summary: The Guardians must go on one final mission to save Rocket's life, uncovering the traumatic origin of his creation at the hands of a twisted geneticist.

beforeWatch.context: The crew's last film together, set a few months after the Holiday Special, with everyone living on the base they bought and Quill in a bad way about it. It pays off threads running all the way back to the first film — especially Rocket's, which has been deliberately left vague until now.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after the Holiday Special

deepDive.plot: When a golden being named Adam Warlock attacks the team on Ayesha's orders, Rocket is critically injured, forcing the Guardians on a desperate mission into his past to find a kill switch buried inside him by his creator, the High Evolutionary — a scientist obsessed with engineering a 'perfect' species and willing to destroy entire worlds of failed experiments to do it. The team frees Rocket and thousands of the High Evolutionary's other test subjects, defeats him, and afterward several members of the team — including Quill, who returns to Earth to reconnect with his grandfather — go their separate ways, closing this chapter of the Guardians.
deepDive.significance: Gives Rocket a long-overdue origin story and a proper emotional resolution, and marks the definitive end of this particular Guardians lineup, making way for a new team under Rocket's leadership.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Quantumania as the next confirmed 2025-set story, following directly from the Holiday Special's setup.

watchFor.name: Rocket's origin
watchFor.thisFilm: Reveals the High Evolutionary's cruel experiments that created Rocket.
watchFor.future: Closes out Rocket's backstory for good.

watchFor.name: The team's farewell
watchFor.thisFilm: Several Guardians go their separate ways by the film's end.
watchFor.future: Sets up a new, smaller lineup of Guardians for any future adventures.

movies.title: Ms. Marvel
movies.summary: New Jersey teenager and superhero fangirl Kamala Khan discovers she has real superpowers of her own, tied to a mysterious family heirloom.

beforeWatch.context: A teenage coming-of-age story in Jersey City, and a very light lift — it needs no homework beyond knowing that the Avengers are famous in-universe, which the show is largely about. Kamala is a fan of theirs, so the more you've seen the more her enthusiasm lands, but nothing is required.

deepDive.plot: New Jersey teenager and Captain Marvel superfan Kamala Khan discovers her grandmother's old bangle grants her real superpowers, tied to an ancient race called the Clandestines who were stranded on Earth generations ago. As Kamala learns to control her powers and juggle her Muslim-American family life, she uncovers her own family's hidden connection to the bangle through her great-grandmother, who fled during the Partition of India. By the end, Kamala's growing powers briefly cause her to swap places with Carol Danvers herself, catching the cosmic hero's attention for the first time.
deepDive.significance: Introduces Kamala Khan, one of the most beloved modern Marvel characters, and directly sets up her recruitment into a bigger team alongside Carol Danvers and Monica Rambeau.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here in the same broad 'a few years post-Blip' period as the rest of Phase Four's later entries, just before Thor: Love and Thunder and She-Hulk.

watchFor.name: Kamala Khan / Ms. Marvel

movies.title: The Marvels
movies.summary: Carol Danvers, Kamala Khan, and Monica Rambeau find their powers mysteriously entangled, forcing them to swap places with each other and team up against a vengeful Kree revolutionary.

beforeWatch.context: A short, light team-up that assumes three separate stories are already in your head: Carol's from Captain Marvel, Monica's from WandaVision, and Kamala's from Ms. Marvel. It does very little to re-introduce any of them. Of the three, Ms. Marvel is the one most worth having fresh.

deepDive.plot: Carol Danvers, Kamala Khan, and Monica Rambeau find their powers mysteriously entangled after a rip in space-time, causing them to swap places every time any of them uses their abilities at once. Forced to team up, they trace the anomaly to Dar-Benn, a Kree revolutionary trying to restore her dying homeworld by stealing resources — including Earth's atmosphere and an entire ocean — using a pair of powerful bracelets connected to Carol's own past. The trio defeats Dar-Benn and repairs the damage, formally becoming an ongoing team by the film's end.
deepDive.significance: Officially unites three of the MCU's most powerful heroes as a working team, and its mid-credit scene teases a Young Avengers-style team assembling from the franchise's younger heroes.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Secret Invasion in the same 2025 stretch, following Ms. Marvel's own ending directly.

watchFor.name: The powers-swapping trio
watchFor.thisFilm: Carol, Kamala, and Monica are forced to literally switch places whenever they use their powers simultaneously.
watchFor.future: Cements the three as an ongoing team.

movies.title: Secret Invasion
movies.summary: Nick Fury returns to Earth to stop a faction of Skrulls, led by a former ally, from launching a hostile takeover of human society.

beforeWatch.context: A slower, colder spy thriller with almost no costumes in it. It's built entirely on the shape-shifting aliens introduced in Captain Marvel and on the promise Fury made them there, so that film is genuinely required rather than merely helpful. Fury has been off-world since Endgame, which the series treats as a character flaw.

deepDive.plot: Nick Fury, semi-retired and living off-world, returns to Earth after a bombing reveals that a faction of Skrulls — led by his former ally Gravik, who's lost patience waiting for humanity to give the Skrulls a new home as promised decades ago — has been infiltrating human institutions at the highest levels, planning a full takeover. Fury and a loyal Talos investigate a conspiracy that reaches into the White House itself, and though they narrowly stop Gravik's coup, the show ends with humanity's trust in its own leadership — and in Fury himself — badly shaken.
deepDive.significance: Recontextualizes decades of MCU history by revealing just how deep Skrull infiltration has run, and leaves lingering paranoia and distrust that colors Nick Fury's role in future stories.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here in the same broad 2025 'present day' period as Quantumania and Vol. 3.

watchFor.name: Skrull infiltration
watchFor.thisFilm: Reveals just how deeply Skrulls have infiltrated human institutions over the years.
watchFor.future: Leaves lingering distrust of Nick Fury and S.H.I.E.L.D. across future stories.

movies.title: Echo
movies.summary: After a violent falling-out with Kingpin's crime empire, Maya Lopez returns to her Choctaw hometown to reconnect with her roots and confront the family and community she left behind.

beforeWatch.context: A direct continuation of Maya Lopez's story from Hawkeye, and a much smaller, more grounded piece of work than anything around it — most of it takes place in a small Oklahoma town. It's five episodes and was designed to be watched in one go. Hawkeye is the only real prerequisite.

deepDive.plot: After shooting her crime-boss mentor Wilson Fisk (Kingpin) during a violent falling-out, Maya Lopez flees New York and returns to her Choctaw hometown in Oklahoma for the first time in years. Reconnecting with the family and community she abandoned, Maya uncovers a mysterious power passed down through generations of women in her family, and ultimately confronts both her own painful history and Kingpin's lingering reach, choosing which legacy — her birth family's or her adoptive crime family's — she wants to carry forward.
deepDive.significance: The first MCU show to center a deaf, Indigenous American superhero, and deepens the Kingpin/Daredevil corner of the MCU introduced in She-Hulk.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here following Maya's introduction in Hawkeye, unfolding in the same broad 2025 period.

watchFor.name: Kingpin / Wilson Fisk

watchFor.future: Continues his rivalry with Maya and remains a recurring MCU crime-boss threat.

episodes.title: Storyteller

movies.title: Ironheart
movies.summary: Back home in Chicago after her time in Wakanda, genius inventor Riri Williams falls in with a crew of high-tech thieves led by a charismatic stranger while chasing the money to finish the armour she can't stop building.

beforeWatch.context: Riri built her first suit as a college student in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever and went home with the knowledge but none of the resources — this picks her up back in Chicago, broke and out of options. It's a street-level story about who funds a genius, and it leans much harder on magic than her engineering background would suggest. Wakanda Forever is the only real prerequisite.

deepDive.plot: Expelled from MIT for selling her coursework, Riri Williams returns to Chicago determined to finish the powered armour she has been building since Wakanda. Short on money and parts, she takes work with Parker Robbins, a charming crew leader whose crimes are pulled off with technology — and eventually magic — that shouldn't exist. As Riri builds an AI companion modelled on her dead best friend, she is forced to choose between the resources Robbins offers and the person she wants to be, and to reckon with grief she has spent the whole series engineering her way around.
deepDive.significance: Pushes the MCU's street-level corner into the collision between technology and magic, and gives Riri the origin proper that Wakanda Forever only sketched — establishing her as the next generation's armoured hero in Tony Stark's absence.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Wakanda Forever, which introduces Riri, and near the end of this phase since it unfolds in the same broad 2025 period as the shows around it.

movies.title: Captain America: Brave New World
movies.summary: Sam Wilson, the new Captain America, gets pulled into an international incident with the newly elected U.S. President when a covert conspiracy threatens to spiral into war.

beforeWatch.context: About a year after Sam took up the shield, and the first film to test that decision at full scale. It's a political thriller in the mould of The Winter Soldier. Unusually, it also reaches back to The Incredible Hulk — the oldest and most isolated film on this whole list — for several of its major players.

movies.timeSkip: Roughly a year after Sam takes up the shield in Falcon and Winter Soldier

deepDive.plot: New Captain America Sam Wilson, without the benefit of a super-soldier serum, is pulled into an international incident when newly elected U.S. President Thaddeus Ross — the general who once hunted Bruce Banner and later pushed the Sokovia Accords — is targeted during a summit over a rare new metal discovered on an island formed from a dead Celestial's corpse. Sam uncovers a wider conspiracy involving mind-controlled soldiers and secret experiments tied to Ross's past, and must stop the crisis from spiraling into war, all while Ross's suppressed rage and past gamma exposure threatens to transform him into the monstrous Red Hulk.
deepDive.significance: Fully establishes Sam Wilson as Captain America on his own terms — without a serum — and introduces adamantium, a new globally significant metal, as a coming flashpoint for future stories.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Six as the direct continuation of Sam's arc from Falcon and Winter Soldier.

watchFor.future: Becomes a globally fought-over resource expected to matter to future storylines.

movies.title: Thunderbolts*
movies.summary: A group of morally gray operatives, assembled by Valentina de Fontaine for her own agenda, are betrayed and forced to work together — uncovering a bigger threat that pushes them to become an unlikely team of antiheroes.

beforeWatch.context: A team film built from people you've met as supporting characters or antagonists in other stories, most of them at a low point. The threads worth having fresh are Yelena's from Black Widow, John Walker's from The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, and Ava's from Ant-Man and the Wasp. It's the most character-driven and least world-ending film in the phase.

deepDive.plot: A group of morally gray operatives — Yelena Belova, Bucky Barnes (now a congressman), Red Guardian, Ghost, and John Walker/U.S. Agent — are each separately hired by Valentina de Fontaine to eliminate loose ends, only to discover they've been set up to eliminate each other. Forced to work together to survive, they uncover an even bigger threat: Bob, a traumatized test subject with god-like power and a destructive alternate persona called the Void, created by one of Valentina's own experiments. After stopping Bob's darker half from consuming the world, the team publicly rebrands themselves as a new kind of Avengers.
deepDive.significance: Assembles a team of antiheroes and former villains into a functioning group, and introduces Sentry/Void as one of the most powerful — and unstable — beings in the MCU, expected to matter significantly in Avengers: Doomsday.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed after Brave New World in the same 2025 period, with its own team formally rebranding by the film's end.

movies.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
movies.summary: Set on a retro-futuristic alternate Earth, Mister Fantastic, the Invisible Woman, the Human Torch, and the Thing must protect their world from Galactus, a cosmic being that devours planets, after his herald arrives to prepare Earth for consumption.

beforeWatch.context: Set on a different Earth entirely, with a retro-futuristic 1960s look, and requires nothing at all — no other film feeds into it. The team already has its powers and is already famous when the film opens, so don't expect an origin story. Treat it as a fresh start.

movies.timeSkip: Joins the mainline MCU timeline by the film's end

deepDive.plot: On a parallel Earth that developed advanced technology decades ahead of the real world, the Fantastic Four — Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm — are already established, beloved heroes when a herald known as the Silver Surfer arrives to announce that Galactus, a planet-devouring cosmic entity, is coming to consume their world. The team races to find a way to stop Galactus without sacrificing Sue and Reed's newborn son, whom Galactus wants in exchange for sparing Earth, ultimately defeating him and choosing to bring their entire world's timeline closer to the mainline MCU universe.
deepDive.significance: Introduces the Fantastic Four and one of the MCU's most powerful cosmic threats, Galactus, while setting up their crossover into the main timeline ahead of Avengers: Doomsday.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed last among the fully released Phase Six films, since its ending is what draws this alternate Earth into the mainline timeline just before Doomsday.
